detail.abstract: A structured questionnaire was used to collect responses from nine participants from India, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. Descriptive analysis was conducted using frequencies, percentages and mean scores. Findings: Overall trust recorded a mean of 4.07 out of 5. Transparency (4.22) and ROI (4.19) were the strongest dimensions, while perceived effectiveness was 3.89 and cost and complexity was 3.44. Understanding advertising settings and performance metrics was a specific area of difficulty. Originality: The study provides preliminary evidence on advertiser-side trust in paid digital advertising among selected small-scale businesses and distinguishes this perspective from consumer-side trust. It also identifies cost, complexity and technical understanding as areas for further investigation. Purpose: This exploratory study examines factors influencing trust in paid digital advertising among selected small-scale businesses, focusing on trust, transparency, perceived effectiveness, cost and complexity, and return on investment (ROI).

detail.abstract: Rural women contribute substantially to the Chhattisgarh economy, yet much of that work stays confined to household and informal settings. Self-Help Groups (SHGs) have gradually changed this picture by giving women a structured way to save, borrow, learn new skills and take up incomegenerating work. This paper looks at how SHGs have shaped women's entrepreneurship in the state, drawing on secondary data from NABARD, the Ministry of Rural Development, DAY-NRLM and related government sources. By January 2024, Chhattisgarh had over 2.75 lakh SHGs under DAY-NRLM, covering more than 30 lakh households, and the state's SHG-bank linkage network has grown steadily for over two decades. These numbers point to a wide institutional base. What the paper argues, though, is that this base alone does not create entrepreneurs-working capital shortages, weak market linkages, limited technology, thin business knowledge, poor packaging and branding, and the sheer weight of household duties all continue to hold back SHG-run enterprises. Moving forward will mean treating credit as one part of a larger package that also includes training, technology, value addition and market access.

detail.abstract: The nursing leadership literature has largely treated the need for professional recognition as either a static trait or a form of immaturity to be outgrown, rather than as a developmental process with distinct functional stages. This paper proposes a two-phase model of motivational transition across a clinical career: an early-career validation phase, in which external acknowledgment functions as a necessary mechanism for calibrating clinical judgment under uncertainty, and a later legacy phase, in which motivation shifts toward the creation of frameworks, systems, or processes designed to operate independently of individual attribution. This paper argues that the transition between these phases is not simply a psychological maturation but a leadership competency with direct implications for mentorship and institutional succession. Senior clinicians who fail to recognize this shift in themselves risk either persisting in validation-seeking behavior inconsistent with their seniority, or-more consequentially-failing to model the transition for junior staff, thereby weakening the informal pipeline through which leadership maturity is transmitted. Conversely, leaders who consciously move toward legacy-oriented practice demonstrate measurable influence through the durability and adoption of the systems they build, independent of continued personal involvement. As an illustrative case, the paper examines the development and institutional uptake of RUISA™ (Al Mohtar, 2026a; Al Mohtar, 2026b; Al Mohtar, 2026c), an operational coherence framework whose design and diffusion patterns exemplify the legacy phase: adoption and embedding into practice occurred independent of, and in some cases without reference to, individual authorship. This case is used not as a promotional example but as an empirical instance of the theoretical transition described, offering a lens through which healthcare organizations might better recognize, support, and cultivate senior clinical leadership beyond the incentive structures typically reserved for early-career staff. This paper contributes to nursing leadership theory by proposing the validation-to-legacy transition as a distinct, teachable developmental marker-with implications for mentorship design, succession planning, and the retention of senior clinical expertise.

detail.abstract: This paper explores the role of smart contracts, self‑executing agreements encoded on blockchain platforms, in automating logistics processes and examines their implications for legal frameworks and operational efficiency. Smart contracts can automate routine logistics workflows such as automated invoice settlement, conditional release of goods, custody transfers, and penalties for non‑performance, reducing manual reconciliation, accelerating settlement cycles and lowering transaction costs. By anchoring event proofs (for example, Internet of Things (IoT) sensor readings, Global Positioning System (GPS) checkpoints, digital signatures) to a tamper‑evident ledger, smart contracts enhance transparency and traceability across multi‑party supply networks, improving dispute resolution and compliance reporting. Researchers adopted a structured approach, gathering and analyzing qualitative data from a wealth of online literature sources and expert opinions. This study meticulously selected 32 peer-reviewed articles spanning from 2004 to 2020, each discussing the Influence of Smart Contracts in Logistics: Opportunities and Challenges. The data revealed the limitations of the growth of uncertainty regarding Smart Contracts in Logistics: Opportunities and Challenges. The systematic approach ultimately provided valuable insights into the Influence of Integrating Smart Contracts in Logistics: Opportunities and Challenges. Crucially, the paper addresses legal and regulatory challenges: questions of contractual validity, enforceability of code as law, jurisdictional issues, evidentiary standards for on‑chain records, and liability when automated actions produce unintended outcomes. It discusses the need for legal recognitions of digital signatures and smart‑contract records, standards for oracle reliability, and dispute mechanisms that integrate human oversight. Implementation risks- data quality, oracle manipulation, privacy concerns, integration costs and interoperability gaps- are evaluated alongside governance solutions such as standardised templates, industry consortia, and insurance or arbitration layers. The paper concludes that smart contracts hold substantial promise for streamlining logistics operations, but realising smart contracts' benefits requires coordinated technical standards, legal adaptations, robust off‑chain data governance, and hybrid modalities that preserve human adjudication for complex or ambiguous cases.

detail.abstract: Supply Chain Management (SCM) is often treated as both managerial practice and an academic construct, yet its conceptual boundaries and theoretical status remain contested. This paper examines SCM as a concept or construct and argues that its development is constrained by persistent definitional ambiguity, disciplinary fragmentation, and the tendency to privilege operational relevance over explanatory rigour. The researchers adopted a structured approach, gathering and analyzing qualitative data from a wealth of online literature sources and expert opinions. They meticulously selected 28 peer-reviewed articles spanning from 2000 to 2016, each discussing the Supply Chain Management: A Concept or Construct - Constraints on Development. The systematic approach ultimately provided valuable insights into Supply Chain Management: A Concept or Construct- Constraints on Development.  SCM is framed across logistics, operations management, information systems, and strategic management; the study highlights how the field’s core ideas are frequently adopted without consistent theoretical grounding, resulting in partial, overlapping, or competing interpretations of key terms such as integration, visibility, resilience, and coordination. The paper also considers how dominant research approaches, particularly case-based managerial studies, can unintentionally reinforce descriptive rather than theory-building outcomes. These limitations are further intensified by the availability of performance metrics that encourage incremental optimization while underemphasizing causal mechanisms and boundary conditions. Using a conceptual analysis lens, the study proposes a set of criteria for strengthening SCM’s theorization, including clearer ontological commitments, explicit assumptions about actors and decision environments, and improved linkage between constructs and testable propositions. The findings suggest that SCM’s maturation as a coherent theoretical domain requires deliberate work to clarify its conceptual architecture and to balance pragmatic concerns with scholarly demands for generalizability, causality, and cumulative knowledge. Ultimately, this paper reframes SCM constraints as opportunities for building stronger explanatory frameworks.

detail.abstract: The analysis concerns the classification of price profiling as processing for direct marketing purposes and the scope of the obligations arising from an objection. A doctrinal legal method is used to interpret Article 21(2)-(3) GDPR, examine CJEU case law and compare selected scholarly views and data protection authorities' positions. Under the interpretation proposed, behaviour-based price selection may serve a promotional function even in response to a customer's enquiry, without a separate advertisement. Personalisation alone is insufficient: pricing based on the cost or risk of supplying goods or services requires a different assessment. The activity's marketing purpose, its being directed at an individual and its connection with profiling must be established separately. The proposed interpretation is supported by the Belgian data protection authority's position but has not been settled by the CJEU for the model examined. An objection covers preparatory operations and further marketing uses of profiling outputs attributed to the consumer, not merely new calculations. This protection does not depend on proof of loss or on the conditions governing solely automated decisions under Article 22 GDPR. Data erasure, pre-contractual steps and contract performance require separate assessment. A prohibition on a particular use of data neither determines the price nor removes the binding effect of an earlier offer.

detail.abstract: Rebranding is a crucial strategy for companies navigating changes in the business environment, ownership structures, and consumer dynamics, as well as regulatory and competitive pressures. This study aims to analyze the interrelationships among public policy, rebranding strategies, brand equity transfer, and product competitiveness within the context of contemporary brand management. It employs a theoretical review approach, integrating perspectives on rebranding, brand equity, brand architecture, glocalization, and public policy. The findings indicate that public policy can act as both a catalyst and a constraint during the brand transition process, while rebranding serves as a mechanism for transferring and reconstructing value from an old identity to a new one. A successful transition hinges on the company's ability to maintain brand awareness, perceived quality, trust, loyalty, and consumer relevance. Although rebranding offers opportunities for revitalization, local product innovation, and marketing efficiency, it also carries the risk of consumer confusion and the erosion of brand equity. Therefore, maintaining consistent quality, communicating the transition in stages, and leveraging brand credibility are vital factors in sustaining competitiveness post-rebranding.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms and blockchain technology to optimise warehouse management across inventory control, order fulfilment, and real-time tracking. Modern warehouses face increasing complexity from higher Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) diversity, omnichannel fulfilment demands, and customer expectations for speed and transparency. AI through demand forecasting, dynamic slotting, route optimization and robotic process automation can substantially improve accuracy, reduce labour costs and shorten fulfilment cycles. Blockchain complements AI by providing immutable, auditable ledgers for provenance, synchronised multi‑party records, and smart contracts that automate transaction verification and trigger workflows across stakeholders. Researchers adopted a structured approach, gathering and analyzing qualitative data from a wealth of online literature sources and expert opinions. They meticulously selected 32 peer-reviewed articles spanning from 2011 to 2025, each discussing Optimising Warehouse Management with AI and Blockchain. The data revealed the limitations of the growth of uncertainty in Optimising Warehouse Management with AI and Blockchain. The systematic approach ultimately provided valuable insights into the Influence of Optimizing Warehouse Management with AI and Blockchain. Our study synthesises current literature and presents a conceptual framework showing complementary roles: AI handles prediction, decision automation and adaptive control within warehouse operations, while blockchain secures data integrity, enforces multi‑party agreements and enables trusted, decentralized visibility for inventory and shipment states. AI‑driven pick‑path optimization paired with smart‑contracted carrier handoffs accelerates fulfillment, and how real‑time sensor data anchored on distributed ledgers enhances traceability for regulated goods. The paper also addresses implementation challenges: data quality and interoperability, latency and scalability trade‑offs, governance and privacy in shared ledgers, and the need for explainable AI in safety‑critical tasks. Regulatory, cost and human‑factors considerations are evaluated. We conclude with research directions including hybrid architectures for edge-AI and permissioned blockchains, standardized data schemas for cross‑enterprise integration, and empirical evaluation metrics to quantify combined AI–blockchain value. The findings aim to guide practitioners and researchers toward robust, transparent and efficient warehouse systems fit for the demands of modern supply networks.

detail.abstract: While much of the literature on education and local investment focuses on research universities, less is known about community colleges. This paper examines how local firm R&D investment affects nearby community colleges, using SBIR and STTR grants linked to IPEDS and College Scorecard data from 1996-2022. Higher local R&D funding is associated with lower net tuition revenue, lower in-district tuition, increased degrees and certificates, modest gains in student aid, and higher post-completion earnings, with no effects on faculty. Effects are concentrated in larger colleges, highlighting community colleges as key actors in local innovation systems.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the integration of robotics technologies into supply chain management (SCM) education, synthesizing empirical studies, pedagogical reports, and case examples to evaluate how curricular approaches develop student competencies and prepare graduates for robotics-enabled workplaces. Researchers adopted a structured approach, gathering and analyzing qualitative data from a wealth of online literature sources and expert opinions. Researchers meticulously selected 34 peer-reviewed articles spanning from 1995 to 2018, each discussing the Influence of Technology on Supply Chain Trends: A Research Overview. Results indicate that experiential, interdisciplinary approaches - project-based learning, industry-aligned capstones, and blended physical - virtual labs - most effectively cultivate core technical skills (automation programming, sensor and control literacy, systems integration) alongside higher-order competencies (systems thinking, human-robot interaction awareness, ethical reasoning). Modular curricular designs (embedded modules, stackable microcredentials, elective specialization tracks) offer pragmatic pathways for balancing breadth across cohorts with depth for students pursuing specialized roles. Institutional constraints - high equipment and maintenance costs, limited faculty expertise, curriculum crowding, and uneven industry access -pose significant challenges, while mitigations such as regional shared facilities, virtual simulators, faculty professional development, and formalized industry partnerships improve scalability and relevance. Equity concerns are prominent: without deliberate measures, resource disparities can create unequal access to hands-on experiences. The review highlights gaps in longitudinal evidence linking curricular interventions to long-term employability and underscores the need for standardized competency frameworks and validated assessments. The paper concludes with evidence-informed recommendations for curriculum designers, academic leaders, and industry partners to implement sustainable, equitable robotics education in SCM programs, and calls for future longitudinal and comparative research to evaluate graduate outcomes and scalable pedagogies.

detail.abstract: The constitutional "right to work," wherever it exists, has never obligated the state to guarantee a job. From France's 1946 preamble to Brazil's Article 6 and India's Article 41, the doctrine imposes an obligation of means, not of result, and it operates by routing individuals toward a labor market that public authority regulates but does not itself constitute. This article argues that this design conceals an unexamined assumption: that the labor market, however imperfect, remains a structurally persistent channel through which the state's means-obligation can be discharged. Large-scale, general-purpose automation displaces labor demand not cyclically but structurally, and no jurisdiction studied here has developed a doctrine addressing degradation of the channel itself, as opposed to a worker's position within it. Using doctrinal and comparative analysis across France, Brazil, India, South Africa, and the International Labour Organization's Employment Policy Convention, the article traces how each system's right-to-work doctrine was built for cyclical, not structural, unemployment, and shows that Brazil's 2021 constitutional amendment adding a permanent income-transfer clause to Article 6 quietly performs the doctrinal move that automation now makes urgent: detaching the protected interest-access to a livelihood commensurate with social participation-from paid employment as its exclusive vehicle. The article proposes the employment-channel displacement distinction, an interpretive tool separating unemployment attributable to inadequate labor-market functioning from unemployment attributable to structural contraction of the labor market's capacity to absorb work, and argues that only the latter category justifies moving the state's constitutional obligation from labor-market facilitation toward direct provision of economic citizenship.

detail.abstract: Federal, state, and international climate-disclosure regimes are not simply diverging in stringency — they are diverging in kind, and this paper argues that the conventional "regulatory arbitrage" framing obscures more than it reveals. Following the SEC's May 29, 2026 proposal to rescind its 2024 climate disclosure rules,¹ federal policy has retreated to a narrow, court-tested financial-materiality standard. Simultaneously, California's SB 253 (with a confirmed November 10, 2026 initial filing deadline)² and the EU's newly adopted Omnibus I Directive³ have preserved — and in some respects sharpened — impact-based mandatory disclosure. This paper's central claim is that because SB 253's $1 billion revenue threshold and the EU's post-Omnibus €450 million/1,000-employee threshold both sit at the upper end of the corporate size distribution, the population of firms actually facing SEC-level federal exposure and the population facing California or EU mandatory disclosure are almost entirely overlapping, not divergent. What looks like an "arbitrage opportunity" in the trade press is, for the roughly 5,000–10,000 firms large enough to matter to any of these three regimes, not a spectrum of choices but a compliance cliff: a firm is either small enough to be exempt from all three, or large enough to be functionally bound by the most stringent of the three regardless of where it is headquartered. We call this the threshold-convergence effect, and argue it should reorient corporate governance strategy away from "which regime is lightest" and toward "how do we build one data architecture that satisfies the strictest regime, since we are not actually escaping it.

detail.abstract:
This study examined presenteeism as a predictor of emotional exhaustion among secondary school teachers in Ile-Ife. It also examined locus of control as a predictor of emotional exhaustion among secondary school teachers Ile-Ife. The objective of this study was to examine the factors that predict emotional exhaustion among secondary school teachers in the town.

A descriptive survey design was adopted for the study. The study was carried out among 150 secondary school teachers who responded through questionnaires in 10 schools. The study population was made up of 15 respondents in 10 public secondary schools in the town. Information was gotten on characteristics of the respondents. The study was conducted on 56 male and 91 female teachers. 

This was investigated using linear regression analysis and the result showed that presenteeism did not significantly predict emotional exhaustion among secondary school teachers, (β = -0.02, t = -0.24, P > 0.05). The model explained that presenteeism did not predict emotional exhaustion. Another objective of the study was to determine to what extent would locus of control predict emotional exhaustion. It was investigated using linear regression analysis and the result showed that locus of control will significantly predict emotional exhaustion among the respondents, (β = 0.34, t = 4.14, P < 0.05). 

The variable explained that 11% of the variation observed in perception of emotional exhaustion among respondents. A joint objective was to assess the joint predictive ability of presenteeism and locus of control on emotional exhaustion among secondary school teachers in the town. Multiple regression analysis was used to achieve this objective and the result showed that the two variables jointly did not predict emotional exhaustion among respondents. Both presenteeism and locus of control explained 34.0% of the variance in emotional exhaustion (β = -8.80, t = -0.99, P > 0.05).

In conclusion, locus of control independently predicted emotional exhaustion among secondary school teachers, while presenteeism independently did not predict emotional exhaustion among secondary school teachers.

detail.abstract: Despite their large effects on the rate of return of investment projects, relatively little research in Economics and Finance examines cost overruns in capital expenditures (CapEx). We empirically explore that gap, offering a model in which simultaneous investment congests the CapEx market. We start by analyzing a project-level panel of investment projects, in a setting with known time-to-build and big-ticket investments: Chilean mining (2010-2025), documenting several stylized facts. First, mining investment is disproportionately volatile, exhibiting pronounced investment waves where various large projects build at the same time. Second, construction cost-overruns increase with aggregate investment. Congestion effects could be equivalent to a ten-percentage-point increase in corporate tax. Third, this congestion is stronger for large projects that are granular for aggregate investment. Fourth, (upward) revisions of CapEx occur mostly after the construction phase has started. These revisions tend to be about unit costs rather project size. Other evidence is also consistent with CapEx congestion around the investment boom. We find construction-laborcost pressure in mining regions during high-investment periods. On the other hand, analysis of earnings-call transcripts and industry sources are coherent with capacity constraints in non-tradable CapEx inputs and specialized Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC). Motivated by these facts, we develop a discrete-time real option game in which firms choose investment timing under commodity-price uncertainty. Importantly, CapEx unit costs rise with aggregate investment. For various frictions, however, a relevant share of large firms act as if they failed to internalize CapEx congestion. This excessively postpones investment and induces CapEx bunching. The model helps discuss policies that may accelerate or smooth the investment cycle.

detail.abstract: This academic essay explores the paradigm shift in executive leadership brought about by digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI). Moving away from traditional technological determinism, the paper posits that AI acts not as a substitute for strategic decision-making, but as an intellectual cognitive accelerator-a digital co-pilot-whose organizational efficacy is strictly bounded by human critical judgment and baseline domain knowledge. Drawing upon qualitative empirical reflections from executive discourse and academic synthesis, the study integrates Socratic maieutics into modern management theory, demonstrating that contemporary leadership excellence hinges on the mastery of inquiry rather than the accumulation of static answers. Furthermore, the essay addresses critical dimensions of organizational governance, cybersecurity, process re-engineering, and lifelong learning, offering a holistic framework for leading human capital through continuous technological disruption.

detail.abstract: The CFA franc (XAF) is pegged to the euro, while the US dollar, British pound, Japanese yen, and Chinese yuan operate under distinct monetary and exchangerate regimes, raising the question of whether their XAF-denominated rates exhibit stable long-run comovement. This paper examines long-run equilibrium relationships among USD/XAF, GBP/XAF, JPY/XAF, and CNY/XAF using a sequential testing framework that moves from conventional cointegration (Engle-Granger, Johansen) to discrete structural-break cointegration (Gregory-Hansen, Hatemi-J) and finally to a smooth structural-change framework (Fourier Shin). The results reveal a marked divergence between system-based and single-equation evidence: the Johansen procedure finds a cointegration rank of one, while every single-equation, residual-based test is either normalization-dependent or fails to find cointegration outright. Notably, the Fourier Shin test-despite confirming that smooth structural change is genuinely present-rejects cointegration for all four normalizations. These findings caution against relying on a single cointegration test when characterizing long-run exchange-rate relationships subject to structural instability, and underscore the importance of distinguishing between system-level comovement and bilateral equilibrium relationships.

detail.abstract: This study examines the transformative impact of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) on the structural evolution of digital banking in India from 2017 to 2026. Utilizing a descriptive and analytical research design based on secondary data from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), and Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), the paper evaluates how UPI catalyzed financial inclusion from passive account creation to active daily digital usage. Grounded in the public JAM (Jan-Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile/RuPay) architecture and private fintech distribution, India successfully converted dormant accounts into active transaction hubs. Between 2017 and 2026, operative Jan-Dhan accounts rose to 92.8%, zero-balance accounts dropped from 24.2% to 5.5%, and total PMJDY deposits grew 4.5x to ₹2.88 lakh crore. Concurrently, annual UPI transactions surged from 0.02 billion to 215 billion, peaking at 23.66 billion monthly transactions (₹29.9 lakh crore) in July 2026, with PhonePe and Google Pay commanding over 78% of the volume. The study concludes that while public digital infrastructure provides the baseline for inclusion, private fintech channels drive sustained consumer adoption. To maintain momentum and security, financial institutions must pivot physical branch operations toward high-margin advisory services, upgrade server and cybersecurity infrastructure, and deepen rural financial literacy.

detail.abstract: Digital platform regulation can alter market outcomes and what researchers can validly observe. We theorize this problem as visibility asymmetry, a condition under which regulation changes platform access conditions in ways that make regulatory intervention and platform response public, while rendering userside behavior structurally unobservable. The enforcement architecture shapes these access conditions and produces predictable patterns of attention displacement in public search behavior. Using six regulatory events across four enforcement regimes, including a within-Texas contrast between an access-change and a later legally salient event without access change, which strengthens within-jurisdiction evidence on the role of platform access, we find that access-changing events lead to a sustained focal-platform attention decline and generally positive workaround-term shifts; the legal-precedent case shows no sustained focalplatform depression, although residual workaround interest persists. The compliance-friction case generates the largest workaround-term elevation in the sample, exceeding all full-withdrawal cases and pointing to heterogeneity in workaround-related attention, where marginal accessibility is preserved. External behavioral reports from the United Kingdom bridge case move in the same direction as our attention estimates. The framework identifies the conditions under which attention functions as a theoretically meaningful but behaviorally bounded outcome in opaque digital markets, and locates enforcement architecture as a central source of heterogeneity in platform governance shocks.

detail.abstract: This study empirically tests for flight to quality in the Helsinki Metro politan Area office market using an unbalanced quarterly panel of 771 properties across 14 submarkets from Q1 2021 to Q1 2026, including 96 Grade A classified buildings. The research design employs a hedonic regression framework where office demand is measured by net take up, vacancy rate and positive net takeup as dependent variables. The estimated OLS and linear probability models progressively control for area and time fixed effects, accessibility and environmental certifications. The results show that Grade A properties exhibit approximately 105 m² higher quarterly net takeup in the baseline model and 165 m² with fixed effects, alongside a 5.5 percentagepoint lower vacancy rate. With additional controls the Grade A advantage strengthens to 151-172 m² in net takeup and to 7.1 percentage points lower vacancy. The results remain robust to a log transformation which dampens the effect of large leasing events, stressmarket tests, and comparisons between noncerti fied properties, where Grade A offices continue to outperform reflecting Grade A classification as a broader bundle of quality attributes. Overall, the findings provide empirical evidence of the prevalence of flight to quality phenomenon in the Helsinki space market over the study period.

detail.abstract:
An organization already operating an access-control or identity and access management (IAM) arrangement, asked to show runtime authorization for the actions of an AI system, can point to capability it has added: finer policies, richer attributes, an ontology, formal analysis of the policy set, a durable record of decisions. Sometimes those additions supply the property the requirement names. This technical note states the conditions under which they do not, and what has to change instead.

The analysis is conditional and turns on which dependencies a change alters, not on vendor, component name, or effort. Three propositions are stated with premises supplied by one stipulated messaging example. First, an enrichment leaves an input deficit intact when the evaluator-visible representation remains identical across the actions the policy distinguishes, or when the added evidence fails the policy's source-authority, origin, integrity, binding, and freshness conditions. Second, an enhancement confined to evaluation leaves a feasible bypass path feasible, because it does not alter that path's reachability, capabilities, or downstream acceptance. Third, authorization does not transfer across an unverified material change: a verdict is bound to one action, one governing state, and the inputs it relied on.

A six-stage progression traces one arrangement of conventional components to an endpoint that satisfies the modeled requirements by design, under three contracts: a decision and input contract, a release contract, and a reconstruction contract. A claims-arguments-evidence matrix states what each claim owes. Three claim levels are kept apart throughout: category membership, adopted-profile conformance, and product equivalence, which the note claims in neither direction. The note does not argue that IAM arrangements cannot become conforming arrangements; the endpoint it describes is one that would, by its contracts and under its assumptions.

The note reports no executed tests and makes no product or conformance claims. The example is stipulated, and the endpoint is a conditional design claim.

detail.abstract: This is a representation-diagnostic study, not a forecasting or model-selection study. The theme is estimand non-equivalence: fit, joint-label recovery, and object concentration are three distinct questions. Football quotes are the frozen demonstration tape, not the object of the claim. Fit is not equal to recovery is not equal to concentration. The paper scores the third. An HMM can unify concatenated variables in one latent chain without concentrating emission support on the blocks the researcher declared. U is that concentration diagnostic on a predeclared object map. Separated U = 1 is structural: that boundary-preserving reference architecture cannot emit across objects. Mixed U can be low, even zero, when a well-specified joint state emits both blocks. That reading can be the correct one. The study uses match-linked football records joined to pre-match market quotes. Mixed is a joint Gaussian HMM on team and market variables; Separated estimates the two object-restricted chains as a structure-preserving reference, not as a baseline competitor. A within-match time-band permutation changes only the declared observation-time labels. The primary sample is one frozen Jiebao Sports (Nowscore) tape of Pinnacle Asian-handicap quotes. After the complete-case rule the three-league panel contains 3,175 matches: 1,140 Premier League, 1,124 La Liga, and 911 Bundesliga. Sequences are team-by-season and are never concatenated across teams, seasons, or leagues. The main empirical result is estimand non-equivalence. The cleanest same-seed demonstration is La Liga at K = 3 and K = 4: validation-selected Mixed exceeds Separated-Market in total validation log-likelihood with selected U of 2/3 and 3/4. At K = 2, the validation-maximizing Mixed seed has selected U = 1 in all three leagues, while the 20-seed mean U is 0.05, 0.475, and 0.525. Those are two operational readings of H2, not a ranking of Mixed against Separated-Market. Simulation identifies the diagnostic: joint-label ARI can approach one while mixed U remains at the oracle value of zero. A train-only PCA encoding changes mixed U without replacing the headline specification. The reading of a latent representation depends on architecture, object map, encoding, aggregation, and threshold.

detail.abstract: Systematic options-trading systems typically specialize in a single analytical lens-technical pattern recognition, volatility surface modeling, or risk-limit enforcement-and combine these lenses informally at the discretion of a human trader. This paper presents the Candlestick-Options Multidisciplinary Decision System (COMDS v1.0), a rules-based standard operating procedure that fuses a candlestick and trend/momentum/volatility engine, a Black-Scholes-based options Greeks engine, a set-theory signalfusion layer, a safety-inspired risk gate adapted from occupational-hazard control principles (NEBOSH), an efficiency gate adapted from sustainability-rating methodology (LEED), and a DMAIC statistical process-control loop into a single composite trade-decision score. The system explicitly treats several of its internal heuristics-a Goldbach-conjecture-inspired signal-pairing rule and a Schrödinger-inspired statesuperposition analogy for undecided signals-as research heuristics and naming conventions rather than as scientifically established predictors of market prices, a distinction the paper argues is necessary for methodological honesty in quantitative-finance research that borrows vocabulary from other disciplines. A backtesting specification is proposed covering walk-forward validation, Monte Carlo resampling, ablation testing of individual signal components, and Pareto-based parameter optimization, culminating in a machine-readable trade card as the system's terminal output. The paper's contribution is the integration architecture itself-a reproducible method for fusing heterogeneous signal types under an explicit risk gate-rather than a claim of positive risk-adjusted returns, which remains an empirical question for the backtesting stage described.

detail.abstract: The 2005 Citigroup "Plutonomy" report argued that firms catering to a wealthy, capitalowning clientele earn a persistent equity premium, but the claim has never undergone a pre-registered, factor-adjusted test. We construct a rule-based, third-party-anchored capitalconcentration tilt (listed alternative-asset managers and S&P Global Luxury Index constituents), frozen before contact with return data, and test it against a capitalizationweighted developed-market benchmark, four pre-registered factor-set decompositions, and a crosscountry interaction with the capital-share trend. In the pre-registered headline window (2013-2026), the tilt does not beat its benchmark net of realistic costs (annualized net excess return-0.35%, 95% CI [-5.52%, 4.82%], minimum detectable effect size 6.55%; the tilt's realized, compounded return is more negative still,-1.26% per annum, reflecting the variance drag of its higher volatility, not a discrepant finding); no factor set leaves a statistically or economically distinguishable residual alpha (all |t| < 1); and the apparent premium is not robustly coupled to the realized capital-share trend across a seven-country panel (cluster t = 1.41 but Driscoll-Kraay t < 1; primary block-bootstrap p = 0.28, permutation p = 0.33). A joint false-discovery-rate correction across this test and a compact companion predictability test (30 primary contacts in total, multiplied five-fold for search) rejects nothing. The tilt's style fingerprint is not a disguised quality or defensive strategy but a regionally concentrated, high-beta sector bet (market beta ≈ 1.3, maximum drawdown-62%) that underperformed during a decade of mega-cap-growth leadership. We report, to our knowledge, the first pre-registered factor decomposition of a plutonomy-style basket, and find no evidence of an exploitable edge.

title: Geometric Necessity of Structural Breaks: Cusps, Slope Jumps, Cascade Transmission Efficiency, and Detection Power of the Unified Shape Function

detail.title: Geometric Necessity of Structural Breaks: Cusps, Slope Jumps, Cascade Transmission Efficiency, and Detection Power of the Unified Shape Function

detail.abstract:
In the k-regime linear switching model, the switching between adjacent regimes is fully characterized by the parameter difference Δθ_j = θ_{j+1} − θ_j. This paper establishes five core results.

Theorem 1 (Geometric Necessity of Rupture): under the switching existence assumption (θ_j ≠ θ_{j+1}), the unified shape function h(τ) exhibits a cusp at the true boundary τ_j*, with slope jump J(τ*) > 0.

Theorem 2 (Local Uniqueness of the Critical Value): h(τ) attains a locally unique maximum at each true boundary τ_j*, and the standardized limits of Chow F/n, Wald*/n, and LR/n share the same locally unique maximum point.

Theorem 3 (Rupture Strength–Slope Jump Correspondence Theorem): the slope jump of the unified shape function h(τ) at τ* is proportional to ||Δθ||_Σ² and the boundary density f_T(τ*): J(τ*) = |h'(τ*−)| + |h'(τ*+)| = 2||Δθ||_Σ² · f_T(τ*) / [F_T(τ*)(1 − F_T(τ*))].

Theorem 4 (Cascade Transmission Efficiency Theorem): in a cascade regime system, if ||Δθ_j||_Σ² + ||Δθ_{j+1}||_Σ² is held fixed and the regime variable densities at adjacent boundaries are equal, the root mean square error is minimized when ||Δθ_j||_Σ = ||Δθ_{j+1}||_Σ.

Theorem 5 (Optimal Effect Size Allocation under Unequal Densities): if the densities at adjacent boundaries are unequal, the optimal effect size ratio is given by the cube root of the density ratio, ||Δθ_j||_Σ / ||Δθ_{j+1}||_Σ = (f_{j+1}/f_j)^{1/3}; when the cumulative distribution values at adjacent boundaries are equal, this optimal ratio is equivalently the cube root of the cusp sharpness ratio: (R_{j+1}/R_j)^{1/3}.

Proposition 1 (Geometric Strength–Detection Power Relation) establishes a bridge between geometric rupture strength and statistical detection power: in the two-regime model, the noncentrality parameter of the Chow test is proportional to the slope jump J(τ*), and this relation is completely invariant to the choice of the reference vector θ_ref.

Definition (Cusp Sharpness) introduces a geometric index R(τ*) = J(τ*)/h(τ*) that depends only on the boundary location and density. Proposition 2 (Cusp Sharpness and Decay Rate) further establishes an explicit relation between R(τ*) and the first-order decay rate of the noncentrality parameter, and discusses the left–right asymmetric decay.

Corollary 1 generalizes Theorems 1–3 boundary by boundary to the k-regime model and points out that the cusp sharpness is a pointwise invariant. Corollary 2 gives a lower bound on the efficiency loss when deviating from the optimal effect size allocation, and discusses its tightness.

The paper derives the explicit piecewise form of h(τ) and its left and right derivatives within the main text; the proofs are fully self-contained. Numerical verification based on real simulation data (MC = 500, n = 2000) confirms the theoretical predictions of the slope jump and the left/right derivatives, and provides an explicit account of the relation between the Chow F mean and the noncentrality parameter.

title: Who Authors (and Owns) Our Minds? Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the Future of Copyright
affiliations: Fordham University, School of Law and Fordham Law School

detail.title: Who Authors (and Owns) Our Minds? Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the Future of Copyright

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: Self funded

detail.abstract:
The groundbreaking Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) are rapidly transforming the relationship between the human mind, artificial intelligence (AI) and the law. Once confined to the laboratories, implantable BCIs have finally entered multi participant human clinical trials and increasingly enable decoding of the neural activity into text, images, speeches, commands and other externally perceptible outputs. As AI-backed BCI systems become capable of interpreting, refining, generating and fixing neural signals into expressive outputs, they challenge one of the oldest assumptions of copyright law: that thoughts remain legally irrelevant until an individual voluntarily externalizes them into protectable expression.  

Copyright doctrine has traditionally rested on a clear distinction between internal cognition and external expression. Where protection arises only on intentional externalization of ideas into an original expression that is sufficiently fixed to qualify for copyright protection. BCIs complicate this sequence. They allow the neural activity to be algorithmically decoded, interpreted, transformed and fixed through substantial AI mediation. This raises difficult questions of authorship and subject matter. When creative expression originated directly from the human neural activity but reaches its fixed form using technological intermediaries like AI-backed BCIs, who, if anyone, is considered the author? More fundamentally, at what point does human cognition become legally protected as expression? Or will these neural outputs always be considered mere manifestations of ideas?

These questions are no longer hypothetical. Copyright law must therefore determine whether such outputs fall within existing categories of copyrightable subject matter, remain unprotectable ideas, or warrant recognition as a new legal category. The answer will shape not only ownership of future creative works but also innovation incentives, investment in neurotechnology, and the protection of individual’s cognitive autonomy.

This Article argues that existing copyright doctrine fails to adequately resolve these questions. Fixation, the idea-expression dichotomy, and traditional theories of authorship were developed in a context where internal cognition was largely separated from external manifestation. Treating decoded neural outputs categorically as ideas could leave individuals without meaningful protection against the unauthorized appropriation or commercialization of creative material derived from their cognition (brain activity). At the same time, extending exclusive rights to neural activity itself risks converting unexpressed thought into property, with implications for freedom of thought, scientific research, and technological development. The difficulty lies in distinguishing protectable expression from cognition without collapsing the two. Thus, looking past the false binary created by the existing doctrine that protects neither innovation nor human autonomy.

The Article evaluates competing ownership claims. One approach would allocate the copyright ownership and associated rights to the neurotechnology firms as users, based on technological fixation, algorithmic selection, substantial investment, Lockean labor principles, innovation incentives and based on Yanisky Ravid AI as agents approach following Work Made for Hire doctrine. The other competing approach attributed the authorship in the individual whose neural activity provides the intellectual conception underlying the work, drawing upon personality theory, biological and cognitive individuality, moral accountability, and the longstanding principle that copyright protects human creativity rather than technological processes.

To resolve these doctrinal shortcomings, the Article develops a purpose-limited, consent-anchored Neuro-IP framework. The framework distinguishing successive stages of neural processing: from internal cognition, through decoded data and AI-assisted interpretation, to fixed expressive output.

title: From Pointwise Elasticity to Path Information: Substitution Acceleration and Exact Aggregation

detail.title: From Pointwise Elasticity to Path Information: Substitution Acceleration and Exact Aggregation

detail.abstract: Standard local substitution analysis is organized around pointwise objects, principally the marginal rate of substitution and the elasticity of substitution at a bundle. This paper introduces Substitution Acceleration (SA) as a hierarchy of invariant local and finite-path objects describing how substitutability evolves along a compensated path: the elasticity path, the local SA field, and a path functional defined as the total variation of the elasticity path over a traversed segment. Agreement at a common bundle in the bundle itself, the marginal rate of substitution, and the pointwise elasticity of substitution does not identify the subsequent elasticity path or its finite-path variation. The elasticity path is transmitted exactly into Hicksian demand and enters observed Marshallian responses jointly with an income channel. The paper's main aggregation theorem derives aggregate compensated quantity-ratio elasticity as an attenuated weighted combination of individual Hicks-Allen elasticity paths and decomposes its path derivative exactly into within-agent SA, heterogeneity-attenuation drift, and elasticity-sorting channels. Aggregation can generate or mask path variation, so aggregate evidence is neither necessary nor sufficient for individual SA. First-order equilibrium matching likewise fails to identify second-order adjustment, while nonlinear composition further transforms curvature. A timing-consistent confirmatory application to European energy demand yields bounded reduced-form evidence. On the 33-country 2005-2022 sample, neither the first-order channel nor the pre-specified nonlinear block is detected for electricity or total energy, and the smooth-transition homogeneity gate does not activate PSTR estimation. By contrast, the discrete rigidity split is detected for electricity (baseline high-minus-low slope difference Delta = 0.000519, bootstrap p = 0.0010) and survives the pre-specified combined pre-trend adjustment (Delta = 0.000480, p = 0.0240), while total energy shows no corresponding baseline split and fails the combined adverse diagnostic. The electricity split is stable to every single-country deletion but materially sensitive to some sample and construction choices. These findings are reduced-form transmission evidence, not structural estimates of SA.

detail.abstract: A stacked imbalance-several adjacent price levels within one bar where trade flow is lopsided in the same direction-is a standard order-flow construction, and the conventional threshold is three consecutive levels. Measured across 115,513 regularhours bars of NASDAQ-100 futures, that threshold is satisfied by 99.94 percent of bars. It does not select a subset; it selects the instrument. Raising the requirement to eight levels leaves a condition met by roughly a quarter of bars, and that condition is followed by approximately 12 ticks of additional price range over the subsequent ten minutes relative to bars of comparable size. The effect survives three controls that each independently account for a large part of the raw association: matching on the bar's own range, which removes volatility clustering; clustering standard errors by session, which removes the inflation from overlapping forward windows; and fixing the detection threshold on a holdout of 60 sessions discarded before testing. It replicates across three non-overlapping spans at t = 5.83, 10.06 and 12.16. The companion measure tested alongside it, volume absorption at a single price, fails at every stage and is reported as a null. The surviving effect is a statement about volatility and carries no direction; at roughly four percent of baseline range it is well inside the cost of acting on it.

detail.abstract: We investigate and quantify the driving factors behind renewable energy generation investments in Australia's National Electricity Market (NEM) between 2012 and 2023. We find that the most important driver of investment in renewable energy capacity has been the federal Renewable Energy Target (a renewable certificate obligation) as well as state targets (in the form of contracts for differences). Operational electricity demand, as well as decreasing capital costs have also contributed to investment decisions and their subsequent commissioned installations. Interestingly, the cost of finance and wholesale electricity market prices were not found to be a significant driver for either onshore wind or utility-scale PV investments. This suggests that either prices at the time of the investment decision do not reflect future expectations, or market price signals alone were insufficient to incentivise these investments. Most renewable generation capacity in Australia's NEM therefore relied on subsidies and long-term power purchase agreements to obtain revenue certainty.

title: Antiwar Is Not Peace: A Pulse-Matrix Audit of Intervention Effects

detail.abstract: An intervention may demonstrably suppress violence without establishing that the altered system is less responsive to every admissible disturbance. This paper formalizes that distinction as a problem of evidentiary support. Using a conventional pulse-matrix representation, historical observations define a bounded disturbance domain over which an intervention effect is supported. A future disturbance may remain within that domain or depart from it. The central result is elementary: non-aggravation over historically supported disturbances does not imply non-aggravation over the full disturbance space. A constant-magnitude directional diagnostic separates pulse size from direction, while a quadratic comparison of pre-and post-intervention transmission identifies where an intervention suppresses, leaves unchanged, or aggravates response magnitude. The title does not define peace mathematically. It marks the inferential boundary of evidence for antiwar effectiveness.

detail.abstract: This submission responds to the Government of Canada's July 2026 public consultation on potential due diligence and civil liability measures to fight labour exploitation in supply chains, conducted by Employment and Social Development Canada. It argues that three design choices will determine whether the resulting regime protects workers and strengthens Canadian business, or merely adds cost and administrative burden. First, coverage as proposed rests on distinctions that do not hold. The operations-abroad gateway turns on corporate form rather than economic reality: it captures the shareholder and releases the buyer, exempting Canadian companies that contract their foreign work to independent providers while attaching obligations to the subsidiary structures Canadian firms need in order to consolidate revenue, realise operational synergies and reach scale from a domestic market of 41.5 million people. Control over a foreign workforce comes from commercial leverage as much as from shareholding. The submission proposes a procurement-based trigger bounded to goods or services intended for commercial resale or integral to core operations; alignment of "conducting business within Canada" with permanent-establishment concepts already used under the Income Tax Act; express confirmation that an entity's international supply chains include services; and deletion of the Option 3 power to exclude businesses by regulation, which invites characterisation as discriminatory application by jurisdictions operating import prohibitions. Second, the proposed civil remedy follows a French model that has now been tested and has not delivered meaningful compensation. The submission would extend standing beyond individual victims to the subcontractors who hold the documentary record, strictly limited to declaratory relief or systemic worker remediation; direct recovery to worker outcomes rather than to the claimant's account; and fund cost-shifting from administrative monetary penalties. Third, evidence produced under a Canadian regime will be worth little unless it is portable. Due diligence conducted under the Canadian framework or a recognised foreign equivalent should establish a rebuttable presumption of compliance — not an absolute safe harbour — under Bill C-35, with interoperable data standards developed through the CETA Regulatory Cooperation Forum. The submission also addresses the exclusion of software and offshore artificial intelligence services from the private-sector limb, in a sector Canada has declared a national priority.

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study, as it is based exclusively on a review and analysis of published literature and does not involve human participants or primary data collection.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was entirely self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: In the last few decades, environmental sustainability has developed from primarily being a concern in ecology to a multidimensional issue involving environmental law, public policy, economic choices, governance, environmental management, and social welfare. The paper offers a critical review of an array of literature focused on the conceptualisation, governing, economic assessment, implementation, and realization of environmental sustainability. The review covers theoretical works, legal literature, policy and case studies of environmental sustainability, and socioeconomic studies in different spatial settings. The chosen literature is discussed in terms of its goals, concepts, methods, evidence, findings, weaknesses, and implications for policy. The studies examined demonstrate considerable variation in their approaches. The conceptual and economic studies highlight the importance of valuing natural resources, determining carrying capacity, taking into account intergenerational aspects, weighing costs and benefits, and emphasizing the link between environmental quality and economic welfare. The field of legal studies informs the study of regulatory approaches, architecture of institutions, enforcement, accountability of businesses, unequal access to information, and important ethical principles and governance issues concerning environmental law. Research aimed at policy issues, in its turn, analyzes the linkages between environmental regulation, green development, technological progress, and finance, i.e. sustainable development. Empirical studies show how the choices made in the field of environmental management can influence costs, the quality of a resource, and the socioeconomic results of economic activity. In the literature, there have also been different references relating to the issue of trade-offs when it comes to discussions of transitions to sustainability. One finding that comes out of reviews of literature is the fact that principles, regulations and policies related to environmental protection do not guarantee good environmental results. In contrast, the results depend on other factors, such as how the political and regulatory framework works, the presence of funds, availability of information, reaction of parties involved in the process, and so on. Therefore, the review compares the main points the authors made in their works and emphasizes the importance of law, policy, and economics in reaching successful sustainability outcomes.

Germany’s statutory pension insurance is financed predominantly on a pay-as-you-go basis and
faces pressure from population ageing, longer pension receipt and changing employment
biographies. This article examines the implications for long-term sustainability and
intergenerational fairness using official data from the Deutsche Rentenversicherung, the

demographic pressure from the capacity of employment, wages, migration and productivity to

detail.abstract: In the Volunteer's Dilemma game, the effort of a single player can provide a public good for many, but in equilibrium, larger groups are less likely to produce even one volunteer. declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to declare
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no support, specific grant, or financial assistance from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or nonprofit sectors.

keywords: Market-based and Basket-based Variances of Inflation

detail.abstract: We show that the description of a portfolio return and variance may model the Laspeyres index and inflation. Inflation is a tool to adjust prices of trades made at different moments to the same time. However, the current theory and the practice for the assessments of the Laspeyres index and inflation overlook this rule. We partially fix this flaw and obtain the equation for the adjusted inflation and derive its successive approximations. We resolve the century-old Walsh's problem of the different trade weights in the basket: "Which weights, then, are the right ones-those of the first period? Or those of the second?" (Walsh, 1921). We apply the transformation we developed for the solution of the similar problem of the portfolio theory and convert the trade weights during the current period so that they coincide with the trade weights of the past period or vice versa. We obtain the time series of values and volumes that model the trade with the basket as with a single commodity. That reveals the identity between the use of the Laspeyres and the elementary index. We introduce the random Laspeyres indices and inflation during the current period and derive market-based variance of inflation that describes the uncertainty of the current and future estimates of inflation caused by the random trades with the basket. We introduce basket-based variance of inflation to describe the uncertainty caused by the random distribution of elementary inflations of numerous goods in the basket. We propose Sharpe Ratio as a measure of the assurance of the current and future assessments of inflation. We refer to Markowitz's advice on portfolio selection and argue that economically effective fiscal and monetary policies, when they aim to manage inflation, should be implemented on the basis of the forecasts of inflation and its two variances.

detail.abstract: I examine whether the adoption of the current expected credit losses (CECL) standard affects information transmission within bank holding companies. Using a differencein-differences design based on within-analyst comparison of earnings forecasts for borrowers and non-borrowers, I find that bank-affiliated analysts issue more accurate forecasts for borrowers after CECL adoption. The effect persists at long forecast horizons, strengthens over time, and increases with the magnitude of the CECL transition impact. Additional analyses show that both macro-relevant and borrower-specific information contribute to the effect. Overall, I provide the first evidence that CECL adoption has unintended consequences for cross-divisional information flows within financial conglomerates, with implications for banking regulators and accounting standard setters.

title: A Global Bayesian Hierarchical Meta-Analysis of the Value of Deep-Sea Ecosystem Services
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Versailles Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines (UVSQ)

detail.title: A Global Bayesian Hierarchical Meta-Analysis of the Value of Deep-Sea Ecosystem Services
detail.abstract: The deep sea remains among the least economically documented ecosystems on Earth, yet it is becoming increasingly central to global governance debates, particularly over deep-sea mining. To our knowledge, this study provides the first Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis of deep-sea ecosystem-service values, using an analytical sample of 119 harmonized estimates from 37 primary studies assembled in DEEPVAL, a new meta-analytic dataset covering the period 1990-2024. To address the pronounced heterogeneity, limited sample size, and within-study dependence of this sparse literature, we estimate separate hierarchical models for stated-preference and market-based approaches, preserving welfare-theoretic consistency across valuation regimes. Under common reference scenarios, we further derive the first posterior-adjusted value distributions for deep-sea ecosystem services, providing full posterior distributions as structured reference points for cautious benefit transfer rather than collapsing the underlying uncertainty into single point estimates. The results reveal two distinct value structures: Minerals rank first in the market-based model (337 Int.$/ha/yr), whereas Waste treatment dominates the stated-preference model (280 Int.$/ha/yr). Regulating, supporting, and cultural services are, by contrast, structurally compressed or absent in market-based accounts. This asymmetry suggests that a purely market-based accounting systematically understates the welfare costs of deep-sea degradation, with direct consequences for seabed mining appraisal and marine protected area design. By distinguishing statistical, predictive, and conceptual dimensions of evidence quality, the framework ultimately makes uncertainty itself decision-relevant and reveals where further research is most needed.

title: Nowcasting incomplete malaria surveillance reports and short-term forecasting in the Peruvian Amazon, 2023–2026
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Nowcasting incomplete malaria surveillance reports and short-term forecasting in the Peruvian Amazon, 2023–2026
detail.abstract: Routine malaria surveillance may be incomplete when first published, limiting both assessment of current burden and short-term planning. We evaluated a two-stage framework combining nowcasting of incompletely reported weekly cases with 2- to 4-week-ahead forecasting in Loreto, Peru. The retrospective ecological study included 183 epidemiological weeks from 2023 through epidemiological week 27 of 2026. Nowcasting used 64 traceable initial-to-consolidated weekly pairs; seven parsimonious models were compared using expanding-window validation in 2023 and frozen before evaluation on 24 held-out 2026 weeks. Forecasting compared naive, moving-average, seasonal, and negative-binomial models with and without climate using rolling-origin evaluation on 84 common target weeks per horizon in 2024-2025, followed by 21 held-out 2026 targets. Mean absolute error (MAE) was the pre-specified primary metric. Initial reports captured a mean 47.2% of subsequently consolidated cases, with a mean upward correction of 169.3 cases. An additive mean-correction nowcast achieved held-out MAE 56.3 versus 199.5 for the uncorrected initial report, a 71.8% reduction, although its empirical 95% interval covered 75% of observations. At 2 weeks, the selected epidemiological negative-binomial model improved MAE by only 0.3% versus the last-value baseline; at 3 weeks, the last-value model was selected; and at 4 weeks, a 4-week moving average reduced MAE by 20.3%. Climate augmentation was not selected at any horizon. Correcting incompleteness in contemporaneous surveillance produced a clearer operational gain than increasing short-term forecasting complexity. Forecasting findings remain exploratory and require prospective, multi-setting validation.
