detail.abstract: Although partisan bias has had a substantially greater effect on survey-based measures of economic expectations over the past 20 years, it has not been found to affect actual household spending. In this paper, we establish that politically driven shocks to individual's expectations influence borrowing decisions. Utilizing credit records for about 600,000 individuals, we show that likely-Democrats increased borrowing relative to likely-Republicans while preserving a similar expenditure following the 2016 presidential election. The results are consistent with changing perceptions about credit access risk. As the opposing party's candidate won, Democrats became more pessimistic about the future and increasingly concerned about access to credit, leading them to draw on existing credit lines and seek new credit.

title: Underwater Heading Measurement with Wave Distortion Removal based on the Polarization Singularity Model and Neural Dynamics​
affiliations: Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Institute of Technology, National University of Defense Technology, Harbin Engineering University and Harbin Engineering University - College of Underwater Acoustic Engineering

detail.title: Underwater Heading Measurement with Wave Distortion Removal based on the Polarization Singularity Model and Neural Dynamics​
detail.abstract: Passive heading information in global navigation satellite system (GNSS)-denied environments can be obtained from the transmitted skylight polarization pattern by underwater bio-inspired polarization navigation. Practical accuracy is nevertheless limited by dynamic surface waves, which continuously alter the local normal of the air-water interface and introduce spatially correlated, non-rigid distortions into the angle-of-polarization (AOP) field. These distortions are further coupled with genuine polarization changes caused by vehicle motion. A wave distortion removal method for underwater heading measurement is proposed by combining a polarization singularity model, inertial angular increments, and quasi-steady neural dynamics. The all-sky polarization structure under multiple scattering is first represented by a corrected polarization singularity model. The model is then combined with inertial angular increments to construct a locally linearized predictor of motion-induced AOP changes. The circular residual between the predicted and measured AOP is used as the neural stimulus, through which wave distortion is estimated and removed online by a bounded response with neighborhood coupling and without inner iterations. At a simulated wind speed of 15 m/s, the heading error is reduced from 0.27° for the best-performing benchmark to 0.11°. In field river trials, the error is reduced from 4.15° to 1.84°. The results demonstrate that vehicle motion and wave distortion can be separated without paired training samples or rich image texture, thereby providing a practical solution for autonomous underwater heading measurement in complex near-surface environments.

title: Conditional Co-Benefits of Rural Solar Infrastructure: Income and Vegetation Responses in China
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Renmin University of China

detail.title: Conditional Co-Benefits of Rural Solar Infrastructure: Income and Vegetation Responses in China
detail.abstract: Can land-intensive renewable energy raise rural incomes without degrading host landscapes? We examine nationally supported village-level photovoltaic (PV) stations in rural China using a 2014–2020 panel of 11,420 villages that links project activation to villagers’ per capita net income, remotely sensed vegetation indicators, socioeconomic characteristics, and environmental conditions. Because all villages in the analytical sample eventually received a station, estimating variation comes from staggered activation timing; estimates are therefore interpreted as earlier-versus-later operation contrasts rather than participation effects relative to untreated villages. Conventional two-way fixed-effects estimates associate PV operation with a 0.0203-standard-deviation increase in a vegetation-based ecological condition index and a 0.0492-log-point increase in per capita net income (5.04%). Joint pre-activation tests do not reject parallel trends, although post-activation event-study estimates are imprecise. Spatial Durbin decompositions show positive direct and indirect income components, whereas the ecological direct component is statistically insignificant and the indirect component is positive. Channel regressions are consistent with lower surface dryness and soil-erosion pressure and show a clearer association with village collective income than with broad firm entry. Point estimates are larger in initially lower-income villages, but coefficient equality is not formally established. The baseline patterns are stable to alternative specifications and randomized timing placebos. Positive grain-output and yield coefficients are treated only as boundary evidence because their pre-activation trends are not flat. Overall, rural solar infrastructure exhibits asymmetric local co-benefits: the income response is clearer than the vegetation response, highlighting the roles of benefit-retention institutions,ecological management, and land-use constraints.

title: Time-Varying Factor Premiums and Exogenous Shocks: Evidence from Cycle-Adaptive Machine Learning
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Time-Varying Factor Premiums and Exogenous Shocks: Evidence from Cycle-Adaptive Machine Learning
detail.abstract: We design a cycle-adaptive XGBoost framework by integrating macroeconomic state similarity weights into the loss function to sharpen the detection of pricing errors under extreme regimes. Using the 2008 Global Financial Crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic as quasi-natural experiments, we apply a difference-in-differences design to quarterly panel data on U.S. listed firms from 2000 to 2024. We find that the 2008 crisis significantly increases 1.53 percentage points per quarter on the absolute pricing residuals of small-cap stocks by relative to large-cap stocks, which is not sensitive to various specifications. The corresponding estimate for the 2020 COVID-19 shock is statistically insignificant, indicating that factor premium failure varies across shock types. SHAP analysis further shows a systematic post-crisis increase in the contribution of the size characteristic, with no statistically significant difference across capitalization groups, suggesting a broad-based change in pricing attribution. The cycle-adaptive model improves predictive stability during tail-risk episodes at the cost of full-sample accuracy. These results suggest that financial shocks accompanied by severe liquidity contraction induce structural breakdowns in factor pricing beyond model misspecification.

title: Who Should Pay for the Wetland? Payments for EcosystemServices and Demand for Government Action in Rural Uganda
affiliations: United Nations Development Programme, United Nations Development Programme, United Nations Development Programme, Green Climate Fund, United Nations Development Programme and KDI School of Public Policy and Management

detail.title: Who Should Pay for the Wetland? Payments for EcosystemServices and Demand for Government Action in Rural Uganda
detail.abstract: We embed an information-provision experiment in a post-treatment survey of a multilateral-funded wetland-conservation project in rural Uganda (N=1,636 households in 16 wetland systems across eight districts) and test how alternative framings of a prospective wetland-conservation incentive scheme shift household perceptions and preferred government action. A short script describing direct payments for ecosystem services (PES) leaves stated perceptions of conservation largely unchanged but sharply reallocates policy preferences: respondents' stated preference for government financial compensation falls by 10 percentage points against a 55% baseline (p<0.01), offset by higher demand for infrastructure investment (+7 percentage points, p<0.01). A long-term economic framing that makes no mention of direct payments produces a near-identical shift; a purely environmental framing produces a much smaller, marginally significant shift on the same margin and moves nothing else. Where responses differ by wetland dependence, they are concentrated among households less tied to the wetland: the reallocation attenuates for the heaviest wetland users, who respond to the PES framing with higher trust and perceived government effectiveness instead. The patterns are broadly consistent with a demand-side analogue of motivation crowding in PES, though the reduced-form evidence is also consistent with Bayesian updating about the fiscal incidence of conservation; we view the demand-side margin as a complement to the supply-side focus that has dominated the existing PES crowding literature.

title: Framing Sustainable Household Waste Segregation in a Small Island Developing State: A Qualitative Study of Local Authorities in Mauritius
affiliations: University of Technology Mauritius and University of Technology Mauritius

detail.title: Framing Sustainable Household Waste Segregation in a Small Island Developing State: A Qualitative Study of Local Authorities in Mauritius
detail.abstract: Sustainable segregation of waste at household level is a focal cornerstone of urban waste sustainable management, besides it’s daily application within rural and urban zones in an upper-middle-income economy, including Small Island Developing States (SIDS) like Mauritius remains irregular in spite of extensive consciousness and regulations. This innovative qualitative study scrutinises how sustainable segregation of waste is stabilised, negotiated and organised, in principle across three different local authorities in the small island: the District Council of Flacq, the Municipal Town Council of Vacoas / Phoenix and the District Council of Savanne which have been selected for reflecting various infrastructural and socio-cultural contexts. By making use of an interpretive approach, 13 in depth interviews as well as three focus group discussions have been performed with members of community as well as waste collection providers. The data have been audio taped, transcribed as well as analysed in MAXQDA thematically utilising a self-critical approach. A number of five associated themes have emerged to capture how sustainable segregation practices are being guided by institutional legitimacy flows and frontline waste collection staff mediation; informal value systems and social logics; material lived infrastructures and momentary rhythms of daily life. Instead of functioning as household stable behavior, sustainable waste segregation emerges as a contextual attainment, negotiated continuously at the household routines interface, carting away practices and local governance arrangements.

title: AI and ESG Disclosure in Indian Listed Companies | Submission-oriented draft ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE QUALITY OF ESG DISCLOSURE: EVIDENCE FROM INDIAN LISTED COMPANIES

detail.title: AI and ESG Disclosure in Indian Listed Companies | Submission-oriented draft ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE QUALITY OF ESG DISCLOSURE: EVIDENCE FROM INDIAN LISTED COMPANIES

declarations.declarationOfInterest: ok
declarations.funderStatement: ok

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in corporate decision systems, risk management, analytics, customer processes and sustainability management, while investors and regulators are simultaneously demanding more comparable and decision-useful environmental, social and governance (ESG) information. This study develops and tests an integrated model explaining how AI capability can influence the quality of ESG disclosure by strengthening firms' ESG data-analytics capability. It further examines whether board technology governance conditions the AI-ESG disclosure relationship. The empirical architecture is designed for Indian listed companies because the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has progressively institutionalised quantitative sustainability reporting through the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR), with mandatory BRSR reporting for the top 1,000 listed entities from financial year 2022-23 and a phased BRSR Core assurance regime thereafter. The model conceptualises AI capability as a higher-order construct comprising strategic AI orientation, AI applications, AI investment, AI governance and AI-related human capital; ESG disclosure quality is modelled as a higher-order construct capturing environmental, social and governance disclosure quality, with emphasis on completeness, comparability, verifiability and decision usefulness. ESG data-analytics capability is specified as a mediator and board technology governance as a moderator. A SmartPLS-based higher-order PLS-SEM design, complemented by panel fixed-effects and robustness tests, is proposed. A 120 firm-year synthetic pilot dataset is supplied solely to demonstrate the analytical workflow; its illustrative results indicate positive direct and mediated associations and provide benchmark diagnostics for the final archival study. The principal contribution is a transparent, India-specific empirical framework linking AI capability with the quality-not merely the volumeof ESG disclosure under an evolving regulatory regime.

title: Quantum Labor Readiness Index
affiliations: Florida Atlantic University - Wilkes Honors College

detail.title: Quantum Labor Readiness Index

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Quantum technologies present themselves as a powerful emerging field with the capability of transforming not only technical computational tasks but also the composition of labor markets. The quantum workforce is lagging behind the development of quantum, with research indicating shortages in hardware, software, research, and business fields within the quantum sector. While advanced economies are developing quantum computing capabilities, education on the matter is lacking. In developing countries, access to education in technological sectors is further strained. To build a quantum labor force, this research proposes a theoretical Quantum Labor Market Readiness Index (QLRI), wherein the capabilities of a country's academic and labor market are measured through indicators of digital infrastructure, human capital, labor market policies, innovation and economic integration, and regulation and ethics to produce a country score revealing the faults within the aggregate. With specificity, government action and industry collaboration can target the specific needs of different countries, thereby efficiently expanding quantum education into previously untapped labor markets.

title: Irreversible Investment in Alternative Projects under Regime Switching
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China, The University of Osaka and The University of Osaka

detail.title: Irreversible Investment in Alternative Projects under Regime Switching
detail.abstract: We study how a firm should choose investment timing and project scale when profitability shifts between regimes. The firm can irreversibly undertake either a smaller, lower-cost project or a larger, higher-capacity project with higher sunk cost. Profitability follows a two-state Markov regime-switching process whose growth and volatility vary by regime. Combining regime switching with scale choice means that a regime shift affects both whether the firm invests and which project it selects. An upward transition from the bad to the good regime may trigger either project, depending on the earnings fundamental. A distinctive result is that, when both projects remain relevant, a downward transition from the good to the bad regime can trigger investment in the small project. The deterioration does not raise project profitability; instead, it can reduce the option value of waiting for the large project relative to immediate small-scale investment. Numerical analysis illustrates representative trigger patterns and how they vary with project characteristics and regime dynamics. The results show that regime shifts shape irreversible investment through the interaction of timing flexibility and endogenous scale choice.

title: Public Perceptions of Discrimination at Large Firms
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley - Department of Economics, University of Chicago and University of California, Berkeley - Department of Economics

detail.title: Public Perceptions of Discrimination at Large Firms

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no known competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors received funding from The Russel Sage Foundation.

detail.abstract: We field and analyze an online survey eliciting beliefs about discrimination and other aspects of recruiting conduct by 164 large firms. Roughly one-third of survey respondents report having put off applying for a job due to fear of discrimination. For each firm, we construct measures of perceived discrimination, hiring discretion, and selectivity. Average beliefs about treatment of applicants with raceand sex-distinctive names correlate strongly with beliefs about broader notions of discrimination. Firms thought to prefer White job applicants are also viewed as favoring older workers, while perceptions of race and gender discrimination are only weakly correlated. Despite substantial inter-respondent disagreement, average beliefs about recruiting biases are nearly perfectly correlated across demographic groups. The race and gender composition of employees explains most cross-firm variation in average gender discrimination beliefs but little of the variation in average beliefs about race discrimination. We compare these average beliefs to experimental estimates of discrimination derived from a large resume correspondence study. Perceived gender discrimination robustly predicts experimental gender contact gaps, while beliefs about racial discrimination are only weakly related to racial contact gaps. Respondents tend to believe that selective firms discriminate more often and that managers have less hiring discretion at such firms. In contrast, experimental race contact gaps are larger at firms believed to grant managers more discretion and at firms believed to be less selective. After controlling for average beliefs about selectivity, average beliefs about racial discrimination become positively correlated with experimental race contact gaps.

title: Macroprudential loosening and mortgage borrower outcomes: Evidence from Ireland
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, KU Leuven - Faculty of Business and Economics (FEB) and Bank of Ireland

detail.title: Macroprudential loosening and mortgage borrower outcomes: Evidence from Ireland

declarations.funderStatement: Francesco Stradi gratefully acknowledges the financial support from Research Foundation Flanders (FWO) Grant 11P7A24N.

detail.abstract: This paper provides novel evidence on the cost-benefit trade-offs of easing borrower-based macroprudential measures. Using Ireland's 2023 loan-to-income (LTI) limit increase for first-time buyers and difference-in-differences estimation, we find that LTI loosening increased mortgage credit by 8.6% and broadened market access for younger and lower-income borrowers. Critically, whether policy easing gives rise to financial stability concerns depends on borrower financial constraints and regional market conditions. In the Greater Dublin Area, where borrowers are more financially constrained, LTI easing led to purchasing more expensive homes and higher debt-service burdens. By contrast, borrowers in other regions used additional borrowing capacity to reduce deposits and strengthen liquidity buffers while maintaining similar housing consumption. These findings demonstrate that the trade-off between market access and borrower financial resilience is conditional rather than inevitable, contingent on borrower financial constraints and regional characteristics.

title: Educating the Opposition: Elite Universities in Authoritarian Russia
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and

detail.title: Educating the Opposition: Elite Universities in Authoritarian Russia

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: GWU University Facilitating Fund

detail.abstract: Does higher education undermine authoritarian stability? While classic theory posits that education fosters democratization, recent scholarship suggests autocrats can co-opt the educational system to achieve ideological control. We reconcile these perspectives by theorizing how elite universities are uniquely able to cultivate critical thinking and downstream economic autonomy, both of which loosen the regime's hold over the most capable graduates. To test this, we exploit Russia's prestigious Olimpiada competition, which grants winners across 24 subjects automatic admission into the domestic university of their choice. Using a novel dataset of over 20,000 participants combined with a new behavioral measure of support for Alexey Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation, we show that Olimpiada winners are significantly more likely to back the political opposition. These top performers were able to attend elite universities, which incubated political dissent not only through exposure to foreign faculty and ideas, but also through the stronger labor market position their graduates command.

title: Regulatory Assets, Regulatory Liabilities and Earnings Quality: Implications of IFRS 20 for Regulated Industries

detail.title: Regulatory Assets, Regulatory Liabilities and Earnings Quality: Implications of IFRS 20 for Regulated Industries

declarations.declarationOfInterest: ok
declarations.funderStatement: ok

keywords: Regulatory Liabilities and Earnings Quality | Research development manuscript IFRS 20

detail.abstract: This study develops an empirical framework for examining how regulatory assets, regulatory liabilities and the quality of regulatory disclosure may shape earnings quality in rate-regulated industries in the transition to IFRS 20 Regulatory Assets and Regulatory Liabilities. IFRS 20, issued by the International Accounting Standards Board in May 2026, responds to timing differences between the supply of regulatory goods or services and the periods in which related compensation is included in regulated rates. The Standard requires recognition and measurement of qualifying regulatory assets and regulatory liabilities and expands information about regulatory income, regulatory expense, reconciliations and maturity profiles. Because mandatory application begins in 2029, a post-implementation test is not yet possible in 2026. The study therefore proposes a pre-adoption transition-exposure model that can be estimated using archival annual-report data. The proposed model contains four principal latent constructs: Regulatory Asset Exposure (RAE), Regulatory Liability Exposure (RLE), Regulatory Disclosure Quality (RDQ), and Earnings Quality (EQ). RAE and RLE are operationalised through balance-sheet intensity, relative-to-equity and relative-to-revenue measures, together with recovery or fulfilment horizons. RDQ captures completeness of regulatory-balance, maturity, reconciliation and risk disclosures. EQ is modelled as a multidimensional construct incorporating accrual quality, earnings persistence, smoothness and discretionary-accrual quality. PLS-SEM is proposed for the latent-variable model, complemented by panel regressions, fixed effects, dynamic specifications and alternative earnings-quality proxies. The manuscript contributes by translating the newly issued IFRS 20 model into testable archival constructs before mandatory adoption. It also proposes a transition-risk mechanism in which larger regulatory timing exposures increase the informational complexity of reported earnings, while stronger regulatory disclosure is expected to attenuate that association. detail.abstract:
This Article proposes ".fn" ("dot first nations"), a new country-code top-level domain (ccTLD) designed to give First Nations, Native American, and other Indigenous peoples worldwide a sovereign, autonomous digital presence built on web3 infrastructure. It argues that the centralized architecture of web1 and web2 has repeatedly failed Indigenous communities, enabling unauthorized harvesting of Indigenous data, cyberattacks on Indigenous health systems, and the proliferation of counterfeit and AI-generated Indigenous art that undermines both cultural authenticity and Indigenous artists' livelihoods. 

Drawing on historical patterns of dispossession, the Article notes that Indigenous peoples have long been denied genuine sovereignty in the physical world, and that current legal protections for Indigenous cultural heritage and intellectual property remain inadequate and difficult to enforce. It then argues that web3's decentralized, blockchain-based architecture offers a unique structural alternative: unlike a merely symbolic ccTLD, ".fn" would let indigenous communities govern their own digital space, authenticate their own cultural works, and control their data without reliance on centralized intermediaries. The Article concludes that ".fn" offers Indigenous peoples a form of digital sovereignty achievable in cyberspace even where physical-world sovereignty remains contested.

detail.abstract: We examine founder CEOs' preference for flexibility through the lens of their financing choices and investigate whether the resulting financial discretion facilitates managerial entrenchment or value creation. Compared with non-founder CEOs, founder CEOs rely less on external financing that dilutes their influence or imposes contractual constraints and maintain larger internal cash reserves. Their lower reliance on debt persists even when positive shocks to real estate collateral values increase firms' borrowing capacity, suggesting that their financing choices reflect a preference for flexibility rather than limited access to external finance. We then examine the consequences of the resulting financial discretion. The market reacts more positively to cash-financed acquisitions undertaken by founder CEO-led firms, and these firms translate R&D expenditures into innovation outcomes more effectively. Collectively, the evidence is more consistent with founder CEOs using financial discretion to facilitate value creation than with managerial entrenchment.

detail.abstract: Cash-flow forecasts are published with no record of their historical error, largely because most forecasting systems cannot be re-executed as of a past date. We present replay-consistent backtesting, which reconstructs the historical open-invoice ledger from a single payment-history export and imposes a point-in-time boundary on counterparty-derived features, and use it to ask what such forecasts can be measured to achieve. Calibrating the generating process to two public registers-a government payer and a commercial purchase-to-pay ledger, whose counterparty signal differs sevenfold-we compute the lowest weighted absolute percentage error attainable by a forecaster that knows every counterparty's true settlement law. That bound is 55-85% at weekly buckets against 7-9% on the horizon total: error in a receivables forecast is overwhelmingly timing allocation rather than amount, and the bound is governed by portfolio breadth and amount concentration as much as by settlement dispersion, so whether a weekly forecast can be scored at all is a property of the book rather than of the model. Replaying the framework on 695,839 observed settlements confirms that structure. Relationship-history leakage proves doubly conditional: understated two-to threefold when measured against a misspecified forecaster, and ranging from nil on a ledger with deep counterparty history to 19% on a thin one. We give a criterion for choosing reporting granularity from properties of the ledger a finance team can measure directly.

detail.abstract:
Research supports that shifting property tax burdens from buildings to land values encourages development and improves equity (Cord, 1985). However, an analysis of these shifts depends on how land and improvement values are assessed. The Cook County Assessor's Office employs LightGBM to estimate parcel assessed values based on property characteristics, but this is only one modeling choice among many. This paper examines how alternative prediction models yield systematically different distributions of assessed value, and consequently different estimates of who gains and who loses under a tax shift. By comparing model predictions and the shape of their resulting distributions, we demonstrate that model selection is a first-order consideration in tax shift analysis, one that existing policy studies largely overlook. 

In this study, we examine how different machine learning (ML) predictions affect the analysis of a simulated transition from a Uniform Tax to a Land Value Tax (LVT). We find that because different ML models capture distinct underlying data structures, the predictions of the assessed parcel values vary, and downstream Uniform-to-LVT simulations yield significantly different outcomes across different metrics used to analyze the shift. These findings underscore the critical need for careful model selection. We caution that future analyses of tax simulations must explicitly account for the predictive variances and inherent limitations of the underlying machine learning models.

detail.abstract: The sense of justice-the conviction that wrongs are made right and merit is rewarded-is the strongest cohesive force of society. When centralized institutions of governance cannot deliver this sense because the cost of enforcing a right exceeds the value of the right itself, social cohesion erodes. Current institutional structures fail to resolve a significant class of disputes in systematically the same way that central planning fails to allocate resources: through information asymmetry, missing feedback loops, and disconnection of decision-makers from the consequences of their decisions. This paper presents the Personix Reputation Social Network (RSN): a decentralized, incorruptible, censorship-resistant communication layer built on Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) that enables pseudonymous participants to publish, verify, and consume reputation information about real-world behavior. The core mechanism rests on three design principles: (1) an asymmetric cost structure where reading reputation data is inexpensive but writing requires verifiable effort; (2) a nondeterministic verifier selection protocol based on consistent hashing that prices radical claims through escalating iteration costs; and (3) a market-driven reputation authority model where private verifiers stake their accumulated reputation on the accuracy of claims they endorse. The resulting architecture produces emergent meritocracy without central coordination and enables a gradual, reversible migration path from existing state-administered systems. The protocol is specified and maintained as an open, replicable reference by the Personix project.

The sectoral method provides additional information when price shocks are concentrated in sectors with large tax-base shares and can improve the interpretation of real revenue for fiscal planning.

Each trade is measured against its own ticker's unconditional return-a compositionmatched null-with calendar-time Newey-West inference. A calibration study with a known zero edge shows this is the only one of three candidate tests whose size stays near nominal (at most 6.8% at a nominal 5%) when signals cluster in time or in volatile markets. Against a zero-return null, 38 of 44 concepts appear significant; against the matched null, with Benjamini-Hochberg control across all 352 concept × horizon hypotheses, none beats random entry at any horizon and none is significantly worse, and an exact rotation test finds no winners either. The largest well-measured point estimates-11-12 basis points over ten days, both liquidity-sweep detectors-have p ≥ 0.23. detail.abstract:
Earnings should be earned. This paper takes that single normative premise, defines earning as adding value, and derives its consequences for the taxation of wealth and of capital income. The return a passive holder receives on wealth, the return the same money would have earned in anyone's hands, is not earned. The return above it is, and so are wages. The resulting tax is a claim by the state on the passive return: in each period the state receives the realized real return on a benchmark portfolio, defined as the aggregate net worth of all resident households, applied to each person's real net worth. The holder keeps the real corpus and any return above the benchmark. When the benchmark falls, the state pays.

Every element of the claim is derived from the premise rather than added to it. The benchmark must be realized, real, and the base's own portfolio; the base must be net worth with netting across a person's holdings; heirs keep the corpus and lose its passive growth; and corporate and estate taxes become redundant. Because the benchmark portfolio is the base itself, the average holder keeps exactly the real corpus as an identity rather than a calibration. The same derivation yields consequences the identities do not soften: the typical holder loses real corpus, owner-occupied housing is largely claimed over a tenure, credit and money reprice to the benchmark, and the state's promise to pay in a crash is large.

The case for the claim rests on desert rather than on the efficiency arguments of optimal-tax theory, and its distributive consequences are stated without remedy. The claim is placed against the rate-of-return allowance, which it mirrors, Allais's capital tax, deemed-return systems, and the benchmark-based inheritance regime, of which it is the general within lifetime form. The single empirical question it rests on, the saving response to a zero after tax normal return, is stated with the test that will decide it. Revenue design, implementation, and responses to the distributional consequences are left to companion papers.

detail.abstract:
This study examines the relationship between loan recovery performance and the financial sustainability of microfinance institutions (MFIs) operating in Bangladesh. Using a structured, five-point Likert-scale questionnaire, primary data were collected from 150 respondents — credit officers, area managers, and branch managers — across several MFIs operating in the sector. Five constructs were measured: Loan Recovery Performance (LRR), Portfolio Quality (PQ), Operational Efficiency (OE), Credit Risk Management (CRM), and Financial Sustainability (FS), each assessed using seven items. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression.
All five construct scales demonstrated good internal consistency reliability (Cronbach's alpha ranging from 0.832 to 0.896). The results show that Loan Recovery Performance (r = 0.620, p < 0.001), Portfolio Quality (r = 0.625, p < 0.001), Operational Efficiency (r = 0.371, p < 0.001), and Credit Risk Management (r = 0.614, p < 0.001) are all positively and significantly correlated with Financial Sustainability. In a multiple regression model explaining approximately 65.5% of the variance in Financial Sustainability (Adjusted R² = 0.645, F(4,145) = 68.76, p < 0.001), Loan Recovery Performance, Portfolio Quality, and Credit Risk Management remained statistically significant, independent predictors, while Operational Efficiency narrowly missed conventional significance once the other three constructs were accounted for. The study concludes that loan recovery performance, portfolio quality, and credit risk management are strong, robust operational drivers of perceived financial sustainability among Bangladeshi MFI staff, and offers recommendations for MFI management, regulators, and future research.

detail.abstract:
Behavior change is frequently initiated but less reliably maintained. Individuals may establish meaningful intentions and begin acting toward desired outcomes, yet discontinue new patterns when initial motivation decreases, competing goals emerge, resources become constrained, or personal and environmental conditions change. Existing theories provide well-developed explanations for particular components of this process, including goal selection, motivational quality, attentional control, self-monitoring, habit formation, environmental opportunity, and social support. However, these mechanisms are often examined within separate theoretical traditions.

This conceptual article introduces the Time to Live (TTL) Model, an integrated self-regulation framework for understanding sustainable behavior change through five interdependent regulatory conditions: clarity, energy, focus, awareness, and support. Clarity concerns meaningful direction and alignment between behavior, goals, and personally relevant values. Energy refers to the psychological and physical capacity available for continued goal-directed action. Focus concerns the allocation and protection of attention in the presence of competing demands. Awareness enables monitoring of behavior, progress, internal states, and changing circumstances, allowing adaptive correction. Support encompasses interpersonal, environmental, and structural resources that facilitate continued action.

The TTL Model proposes that sustainable behavior change depends not solely on initial motivation, intention strength, or willpower, but on the coordinated functioning of these five conditions over time. Its distinctive theoretical contribution is configurational: a substantial deficit in one component may become a regulatory bottleneck, destabilizing behavior maintenance even when other components remain relatively strong. The model further conceptualizes lapses not as definitive failures but as regulatory information that can activate monitoring, adaptation, and behavioral recovery. Drawing on research in self-regulation, goal-setting, self-concordance, subjective vitality, attentional control, implementation intentions, progress monitoring, habit formation, psychological flexibility, goal adjustment, and social support, the article develops testable propositions and outlines a program for empirical validation.

This paper asks a narrower and more tractable question: within the remaining, non-silicon share of the rack and its supporting facility-specifically the liquid-cooling loop, thermal-interface materials, coolant-distribution hardware, and fluid chemistry-which manufacturing sub-segments are structurally reachable by an entrant capitalized between ₹1 crore and ₹10 crore (approximately US$120,000-1.2 million), and under what certification, subsidy, and channel conditions? Drawing on a rack-and facility-level bill-of-materials decomposition, a comparative screen of sixteen candidate manufacturig categories, and a review of India's post-2020 industrial-policy instruments-the Production Linked Incentive (PLI), Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), and India Semiconductor Mission (ISM)-the analysis identifies four candidates (liquid-cooling balance-of-plant, thermal-interface converting and kitting, in-rack coolant-distribution-unit assembly, and coolant/fluid services) that combine low capital intensity, inherited or attainable certification, and gross margins above the 7-14% typical of commodity Indian contract manufacturing. The paper situates this finding within the import-substitution-industrialization literature and argues that it identifies a policy mechanism-localization obligations cascading downward through a supply chain-that is analytically distinct from, and understudied relative to, the tariff-and subsidy-centered instruments that literature has traditionally evaluated.

detail.abstract:
Scientific representations can become causally embedded in the worlds they describe. Models enter markets, classifications organize populations, measurement rules structure incentives, and predictions can alter the environments from which later evidence is drawn. Recent philosophy of science has treated these phenomena under the headings of reactivity and performativity. This paper isolates a further diachronic problem: the causal consequences of epistemic intervention and the information required to identify their historical contribution need not persist at the same rate.

I develop an architecture of epistemic provenance non-identifiability that distinguishes causal-state transmission, through which consequences persist in an inherited world, from causal-provenance transmission, through which query-discriminating information about their origins is preserved. Four regimes of historical identifiability separate incomplete history from genuine underdetermination. An exact-collapse proposition then shows that when query-divergent histories become informationally equivalent at a transmitted state, and later endogenous evidence depends on prior history only through that state, downstream observation cannot recover the lost distinction.

The mathematical ingredients are standard; no new result in information theory, probability theory, or partial-identification theory is claimed. The contribution is architectural and epistemological: identifiability itself can change historically when causal effects and the provenance required to attribute them are transmitted through different channels. A brief illustration from performative prediction identifies the kinds of deployment records whose preservation can condition later causal attribution.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the Dimensional Transformation Theory (also referred to as the Hierarchy Transition Hypothesis), a novel theoretical framework that reconceptualizes trading volume not as a monolithic indicator but as a multi-level, role-shifting signal within financial markets. Drawing on 77,825 daily observations spanning 28 Shenwan primary industries and 26 CSI 300 constituent stocks from 2020 to 2026, we propose and test four core hypotheses:
(H1) Hierarchy Conduction—that volume signals propagate from macro-level (broad market) to meso-level (industry) to micro-level (individual stock) with measurable time lags; 
(H2) Role Transition—that the dominant explanatory role of volume shifts systematically across market regimes, with individual-stock volume dominating in bull markets, industry-level volume prevailing in oscillating markets, and broad-market volume asserting dominance in bear markets;
(H3) Resonance Returns—that stocks exhibiting simultaneous volume alignment across all three levels generate statistically and economically significant excess returns; 
(H4) Cross-Level Synchronization—that the degree of volume synchronization across levels exhibits nonlinear threshold effects and significant market-state heterogeneity.
Employing Granger causality tests, VAR impulse response functions, and Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions, we find strong support for H2 and H3, partial support for H1 (with 1–4 day conduction lags from broad-market to industry level), and conditional support for H4 (with synchronization breaking down during bear markets). A six-fold robustness battery and out-of-sample validation through the Six-Dimension Resonance Strategy Matrix (versions V5.2, V5.3, V5.4 Pro, V5.5, and Broad-Market V1.0) across 10 backtests confirm the framework's empirical validity. The Dimensional Transformation Theory offers a unified lens for understanding volume behavior across market hierarchies and provides actionable implications for multi-level trading strategies, risk management, and market regime detection.

detail.abstract: Purpose: Institutions play an important role in stimulating economic growth of the country. They create frameworks for economic activity through restrictions that shape human interaction. Economic growth is a complex process influenced by many factors, including the quality of institutions. The main goal of this paper is to examine the correlation between institutions and economic growth in Bosnia and Herzegovina (hereinafter referred to as B&H). Methodology: The paper applies both descriptive and inferential statistics, along with various scientific research methods. It examines the correlation between selected indicators and conducts regression analysis to establish the relationship between indicators of economic growth and the institutional quality in Bosnia and Herzegovina during the period from 2002 to 2022. The central research question is: Does institutional quality determine economic growth in B&H? Specifically, which elements of institutional quality have a positive impact, and which have a negative impact on GDP? Additionally, which elements have the strongest correlation with changes in GDP in B&H? Results: Results show that institutional quality is declining, while economic growth exhibits modest positive trends. Correlation analysis revealed a statistically significant relationship between Voice and Accountability, Regulatory Quality, Rule of Law, and Control of Corruption and Economic Growth in B&H, while regression analysis further determined that Regulatory Quality has the greatest impact on economic growth in B&H. Conclusion: One of the key challenges for economically, politically, socially, and religiously complex, small, and open countries like Bosnia and Herzegovina is the development of adequate, efficient, transparent, and corruption-free institutions.

detail.abstract: Forecasting real-world events requires reasoning under uncertainty from information available at a fixed cutoff. Recent work has improved how large language models (LLMs) retrieve evidence and produce probabilistic forecasts, but each question is treated independently even when similar events recur. Resolved occurrences carry experience for later forecasts, yet past outcomes and case summaries do not preserve the relationships that made an earlier occurrence informative. We develop ReFoRM (Recurrent-event Forecasting with Reasoning Memory), which organizes reasoning from resolved events into predictive paths, retrieves relevant paths for a later occurrence, and reconstructs their relations using evidence at the new forecast cutoff. We evaluate ReFoRM on the Recurring Financial Events Set, which contains 300 questions across 40 recurring financial event families and uses earlier occurrences as hindsight for 100 forecast targets. Across five LLMs and six baselines, ReFoRM improves categorical and probabilistic forecasting performance. Further analyses show that validating historical relations with current evidence and reconstructing them enhances forecasting. Reasoning evaluation also demonstrates stronger evidence grounding, logical validity, and mechanism specificity.

detail.abstract: We study optimization and decentralized stochastic control problems on large sparse graphs, with graphings serving as the limiting objects under local-global convergence. For a broad class of graph optimization problems whose objective aggregates local costs, we prove convergence of the optimal values to their graphing counterparts and derive first-order optimality conditions for the limiting problem. This convergence applies to independence, maximum-cut, and dominating-set densities. We then extend the framework to controlled diffusions whose dynamics and information are local to each vertex, while interactions between neighboring vertices enter through the running and terminal costs. In this setting, we establish convergence of the optimal values under local-global convergence and derive a stochastic maximum principle for the limiting graphing control problem.

detail.abstract: Standard measures of institutional quality emphasize formal, rule-based governance. Yet, prominent postwar growth episodes occurred under diverse institutional arrangements, suggesting that the relationship between measured institutions and economic performance may vary by stage of development. We examine this possibility in three settings. In the country sample of Acemoglu et al. (2001), institutions-income associations are positive and statistically significant across stages, yet weak first-stage relationships limit causal inference in the high-rural subsample; in the subnational data of Mitton (2016), the associations are generally insignificant in countries with high rural-population shares. Our main analysis combines regional control of corruption with GDP per capita growth across 1,369 subnational regions in 155 countries from 1995 to 2022. We find that better regional control of corruption predicts faster medium-run growth in countries with lower initial rural shares, while the corresponding association in countries with higher initial rural shares is much weaker and not significant. Pooled interaction estimates show statistically significant differences at similar medium-run horizons. Across alternative rural-share cutoffs, the low-rural estimates remain positive, while the high-rural estimates are smaller and sometimes negative. These findings offer supportive evidence to the hypothesis that returns to measured institutions depend on the stage of development. We discuss mechanisms and implications.

detail.abstract: Historic coins are among the last major collectible classes without a portfolio analysis based on transaction prices. This paper asks what allocation to historic coins an investor should have held alongside thirteen liquid benchmark assets, using the Global Numismatic Assets Index, the first monthly transaction-based international index for coins: 77 coin types, 5,588 auction records, 2006 to 2025. Coin inputs enter the optimisation corrected throughout: volatility is adjusted for the smoothing that infrequent trading imposes, co-movement is taken from summed-lag estimates rather than contemporaneous correlations, and transaction costs of 25 per cent round trip are amortised over a twenty-year holding. On the index's published statistics, uncorrected, the optimiser would assign coins 35 per cent of a diversified portfolio; corrected and net of costs, the mean-variance optimum holds 6.2 per cent. A tail-risk optimisation places coins far higher, because in the worst months of a diversified portfolio coins held their value while equities, property, and both precious metals fell. Against five standard starting portfolios, from a global 60/40 to an endowment-style allocation, a coin sleeve net of costs ranks third or fourth among fourteen candidate additions, raises every portfolio's Sharpe ratio, and cuts realised maximum drawdowns by roughly a fifth. The answer to the allocation question is a partition with concrete coordinates. Coins belong to an investor who holds a portfolio concentrated in conventional assets and can wait: against the five standard portfolios coins enter at holding periods of eight to eleven years at the central estimates, and the sleeve is larger the more the portfolio is concentrated in conventional assets. Coins do not belong in the portfolio in three cases: where gold and other real assets already do the diversifying and leave coins no room, where the return target can be met only by the highest-return assets, or where the investor cannot hold long enough to recover the transaction costs.

detail.abstract:
The paper evaluates the types of environmental taxes applied within the extractive sector, examine their effect on corporate environmental behavior and compliance and assess their effectiveness in contributing to sustainable development outcomes.

The paper adopts a qualitative research method based on secondary data analysis. Data were obtained from institutional sources including reports from the Environmental Protection Agency, Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) Ghana, Ministry of Finance publications and other relevant policy documents covering the period 2020-2024. The data were analyzed using descriptive and thematic analysis techniques to identify patterns in environmental fiscal policy implementation, compliance behavior and sustainability outcomes within the extractive sector.

The findings reveal that environmental taxation in Ghana is mainly implemented through legally established regulatory frameworks including environmental permit fees, pollution charges, environmental monitoring fees and reclamation bonds.

It concludes that while environmental taxation represents an essential policy tool for promoting sustainable development within Ghana’s extractive sector, it is not sufficient as a standalone mechanism. Its effectiveness depends broadly on strong institutional frameworks, effective enforcement mechanisms and transparent fiscal governance. The research recommends reinforcing institutional capacity, enhancing regulatory coordination and improving transparency in environmental revenue management to boost the sustainability benefits of environmental taxation.

detail.abstract: Soil-health indicators are commonly interpreted against benchmarks, yet universal thresholds can confound management effects with inherent differences in soil and climate. Ecological reference conditions provide an estimate of soil potential but may represent endpoints that are difficult to attain within agricultural management timescales. We assessed whether land-use and management conditions could instead be organized into a Hierarchical Land Classification (HLC) and used to derive incremental, environmentally contextualized soil targets. A literaturederived database was classified into five hypothesized states: ecological reference (A), advanced recovery/low disturbance (B), soil-building transition (C), production baseline (D), and degraded land (E). The primary mixed-effects analysis included 1,059 soil organic carbon (SOC) observations from 105 study and accounted for climate, sampling depth, and study-level variability. Soil organic carbon followed a strong but nonlinear hierarchy. Relative to the production baseline, adjusted SOC was 50.0% greater in A, 27.0% greater in B, 24.9% greater in C, and 30.2% lower in E. Adjacent contrasts supported an empirical ordering of A > B ≈ C > D > E, with B and C not statistically distinguishable. Cropland soil-building practices collectively increased SOC by 24.2% relative to production baselines, although responses varied among management pathways. Following cropland retirement, SOC increased approximately 8.5% per additional decade. The HLC pattern remained robust within the 0-30 cm surface soil. These findings demonstrate that land condition can be represented by a transferable relative hierarchy, but numerical SOC targets should not be universal or equally spaced. Instead, ecological potential, environmental context, management pathway, and current condition can be combined to define empirically supported, incremental targets between production and reference states.

detail.abstract: This submission responds to the Government of Canada's July 2026 public consultation on the regulatory approach under Bill C-35, An Act respecting the prohibition of the importation of goods produced by forced labour, conducted by Global Affairs Canada and the Canada Border Services Agency. The regulations will determine what an importer must produce when a shipment is stopped at the border. That question cannot be resolved until Canada decides what a legally compliant supply chain record looks like — a foundational issue left unaddressed across the two concurrent consultations. Bill C-35 is moving on a compressed timeline driven by pressures outside Canada, including the July 2026 Section 301 determination by the Office of the United States Trade Representative and the resulting tariff on non-exempt Canadian exports. If the border regulations establish a rigid, isolated standard designed solely for customs clearance, that standard will foreclose the broader due diligence architecture, and Canada's trade security will continue to rest on external pressure rather than on a portable data standard built around its own priorities. The submission advances two principal claims. First, neither an uncoordinated public registry of suspect producers nor a post-detention evidentiary demand can serve as a workable operational standard. Canada should publish objective criteria for listing and removal, bias the unit of listing toward individual producers and facility locations rather than country-wide designations that punish compliant suppliers, reject blanket corporate safe harbours, and adopt instead a rebuttable presumption of compliance anchored in a portable, multi-tier supply chain record — while preserving the CBSA's power to act on specific, actionable intelligence. A cost-recovery charge compliant with Article VIII of the GATT, rather than an ad valorem levy, should shift verification costs to importers who leave the work to the state. Second, an import prohibition restricted to physical cargo ignores the economic reality of digital trade. Software development and artificial intelligence training outsourced to developers in emerging markets fall outside the proposed regime entirely, in a sector Canada has designated a national priority and in which it has asserted system sovereignty. Sovereignty over a system means being able to account for every input that built it. The submission argues for digital provenance standards developed in coordination with the Sovereign Technology Alliance and interoperable ledger standards through the CETA Regulatory Cooperation Forum.

detail.abstract: European capital markets structurally repriced defence-sector equity between late 2021 and 2026. Using the full STOXX 600 membership history, we show that a long-short portfolio of European defence firms, which earned no abnormal returns before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, delivered an annualised five-factor alpha of roughly 26% afterwards. Endogenous break tests date the regime shift to November and December 2021, two to three months before the invasion: markets repriced the sector on anticipation, not on the event itself. Two methodologically distinct implied-cost-of-capital estimators show that the required return of the typical defence firm fell by roughly 250 to 300 basis points relative to the rest of the market, a compression concentrated in pure-play names and smaller in value-weighted terms. This compression capitalises into about a quarter of the cumulative abnormal return; the sequential arrival of fiscal cash-flow news explains the remainder. We interpret the episode as the release of an ESG-exclusion constraint, the mirror image of green-asset repricing, and direct evidence that institutional exclusion at scale moves required returns.

detail.abstract:
In recent years, Indian courts have progressively developed a freestanding right of publicity or personality right, protecting names, likenesses and other indicia of identity. This chapter argues that the resulting jurisprudence is doctrinally unstable. Although courts justify protection by reference to privacy and autonomous self-definition, the emerging infringement architecture is distinctly proprietary: it privileges celebrity status, commercial value and the misappropriation of fame, while permitting assignment. These features of the right sit uneasily with the right’s dignitary foundations. 

Tracing the development of Indian image-rights jurisprudence and its selective transplantation of US doctrine, the chapter demonstrates that this tension generates inconsistent answers to fundamental questions concerning who may claim protection (is it only celebrities?), whether the right is transferable or inheritable, and what conduct should constitute infringement. It argues against resolving these inconsistencies by further propertising personal identity. Instead, Indian law should return image protection to its privacy foundations and develop an autonomy-based tort available to celebrities and ordinary individuals alike. Under this framework, liability would turn not merely on appropriation without permission, but on actionable harm including compelled association, false endorsement, destruction of anonymity and reputational damage. Such an approach can address contemporary digital harms, including unauthorised deepfakes, while preserving appropriate space for news reporting, criticism, parody, artistic expression and other legitimate speech interests.

detail.abstract: Dense regulation and weak standardization have coexisted in Nigeria’s oil and gas sector for long enough that the contradiction has stopped surprising people. The Petroleum Industry Act 2021 gave us the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) and the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). The Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry Content Development Act 2010 (NOGICD Act) gave us the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB). The Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) governs national standards. The framework is, on paper, substantial. Yet every practitioner who has advised an operator in this sector, and every international investor who has financed one, knows what none of these institutions will say out loud: International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO) management system standards are demanded across the industry every day and are invisible in every piece of Nigerian petroleum regulation. This paper names that condition the compliance phantom — a standard that exists in practice but not in law — and its direct consequence, the compliance conundrum: where demonstrated compliance earns no regulatory reward, and its absence attracts no regulatory penalty. The infrastructure to close this gap already exists — in the Nigeria National Accreditation System (NiNAS), SON, NCDMB, NMDPRA, NUPRC, and the Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas Limited (NLNG). Nigeria does not need new institutions, new legislation, or foreign models. It needs the regulatory will to connect what it already has, and a Nigerian Petroleum Standards Accreditation Framework (NPSAF) to give that will, legal form. The reform pathway this paper proposes does not wait on the National Assembly. Each tier can be implemented through powers the relevant institutions already hold.

detail.abstract: Purpose-Grid connection positions are normally treated as technical approvals or administrative places in a queue. This paper develops a strategic-management account of those positions as contingent control rights whose value derives from the ability to defer, stage, modify, combine, transfer indirectly through project transactions, or abandon investment under uncertainty. It integrates realoptions theory, the resource-based view and dynamic-capabilities theory with documentary interpretation of the public rules governing Great Britain's reformed electricity-connections regime. Its value is not intrinsic to queue rank. It is co-produced by location, timing, technology, evidence of readiness, strategic alignment and the developer's capacity to keep multiple development pathways open. detail.abstract: Contemporary AI-safety discourse often places advanced AI in the exceptional position of a potential responsible subject, as if autonomy, complexity, and unpredictability required a new philosophy of governance and responsibility. This paper argues for taking AI off that pedestal and placing it in a more accurate governance niche: AI is an intellectual tool that augments the intelligence of natural or juridical persons, not the terminal bearer of responsibility. As with automobiles, aircraft, and other complex technologies, introducing a tool may redistribute duties and liability among users, providers, manufacturers, and deployers, but responsibility can be allocated around the tool, not into the tool itself. AI safety should therefore be governed by extending existing logics of responsibility allocation, licensing, and control of dangerous capabilities rather than by inventing a jurisprudence for an unprecedented alien intelligence. Regulatory intensity should follow the consequential capabilities that responsible persons can obtain through AI, robots, and other tools; hazardous materials, dangerous equipment, hazardous facilities, and access to their control should remain subject to the familiar logic of licensing, containment, permission boundaries, auditing, and liability used for high-risk activities. Intelligence is not itself a dangerous capability; the relevant question is what dangerous capabilities intelligence can access and control. The governance of dangerous capability should not be mistaken for the governance of intelligence itself.

detail.abstract: Mainstream economic classifications divide economic activities according to final product form or industrial sector affiliation. The dispute over "Factoryless Goods Producers" (FGP) in statistical circles has already exposed the distortion of this classificatory coordinate: Apple, Nvidia, Nike, and similar firms are counted as manufacturing, although they themselves do not engage in large-scale manufacturing. However, the focus of the FGP literature is "whether such firms should be classified into manufacturing or wholesale"-that is, finding a new cell within the old coordinate, without questioning the coordinate itself. Research on functional specialisation in the trade literature has demonstrated the feasibility of dividing economic activities by function, but its object of division is occupations and trade flows; it has not extended to firm classification and national economic structure. This paper connects the two literatures and proposes a functional classification framework for economic structure analysis-the Four-Layer Functional Model: instead of dividing by final product form, it divides economic activities according to the form of their core output and their functional position in the production system into Basic Resource Function (V1), Hard-Entity Production Function (V2), Soft-Entity Production Function (V3), and Service Realization and Organization Function (V4). It provides executable classification rules based on the principle of "one's own core output," rules for handling composite types, and rules for boundary cases. Exploratory applications at the firm, industry, and national levels show that the framework can identify systematic classification mismatches invisible under traditional classification. The paper further derives five falsifiable propositions from the framework and provides a staged mapping scheme from firm level to national level. This paper is a theory-building study; cases serve to illustrate classification and explain mechanisms, not to perform statistical inference.

detail.abstract: Remote work relocated the origin of urban consumer spending without eliminating it. This paper asks whether that relocation is associated with improved retail occupancy in neighborhoods gaining residential spending origins, and whether any operating improvement is accompanied by higher conditional transaction prices. Using a balanced panel of 13,826 New York City parcels, I find that a ten-percentage-point shift in surrounding floor area from office to residential use is associated with 0.57 to 0.96 percentage points less growth in reported storefront vacancy after 2019, the lower figure holding reported storefront counts fixed. Independent Census Business Register data show a corresponding post-2019 pattern for food-service establishments, though the design remains observational. detail.abstract: In medical image segmentation, Black-Box Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (BBSF-UDA) has become increasingly important due to real-world constraints such as data privacy, restricted access to model internals, and regulatory limitations that prohibit model modification. While existing BBSF-UDA methods avoid accessing source model parameters, they typically rely on complex auxiliary networks or memory-heavy components, leading to high computational costs and poor scalability, especially with large foundation models like SAM. These limitations hinder practical deployment in resource-constrained clinical environments. To address this, we propose BlackFDP, a lightweight BBSF-UDA framework that bypasses the need for heavy auxiliary networks or full model duplication. Instead, we optimize only lightweight trainable components using black-box gradient estimation based solely on model outputs. Specifically, we introduce the Fourier Dual Prompt (FDP), which injects frequency perturbations into the input image through two Fourier visual prompts, including a domain-specific prompt and an input-specific prompt. These prompts are trained end-to-end via black-box optimization, allowing effective adaptation without accessing gradients or source data. Extensive experiments across medical segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance while dramatically reducing computational and memory costs. Moreover, we show that the framework seamlessly adapts foundation models like SAM using only API access, highlighting its strong potential for real-world clinical adaptation.

detail.title: BT U-Net: Direct Spectral Bottleneck Reconstruction for Medical Image Segmentation
detail.abstract: Medical image segmentation requires both precise local boundary preservation andeffective global structural modeling. Although U-Net remains a widely used baselinefor biomedical segmentation, its convolutional operations mainly aggregate localneighborhood information, which can limit its ability to represent irregularlesions, blurred boundaries, and long-range structural dependencies. To address this limitation, this paper proposes BT U-Net, a direct spectral bottleneck reconstruction framework for medical image segmentation. The proposed method keeps the standard U-Net encoder--decoder structure but replaces the deepest bottleneck feature with adirectly reconstructed spectral representation. Specifically, the bottleneck feature is transformed into the Fourier domain, modulated through learnable amplitude and phase responses, mixed across spectral channels, and reconstructed before being passed to the decoder. This design concentrates global spectral interaction at the deepest low-resolution bottleneck stage of U-Net without introducing attention or transformer branches. Experiments on polyp segmentation datasets, an additional endoscopic segmentation dataset, and a non-polyp medical image segmentation dataset show that BT U-Net improves the standard U-Net-family baselines on challenging segmentation benchmarks and remains competitive on ISBI-2012. Ablation studies further show that direct bottleneck reconstruction is more effective than a residual Fourier-control variant. These results support BT U-Net as a compact spectral bottleneck enhancement for strengthening encoder--decoder medical segmentation networks.

detail.abstract: A positively weighted composite of regressors can have a negative regression coefficient even when every component has a strictly positive structural effect. This paper examines this possibility when the weights vary across observations. Under conditional exogeneity, we show that the sign of the population composite coefficient is determined by whether the composite constructed from the conditional mean weights moves with or against the structural index. This result does not require the regressors to be centered. Variation in weights around their conditional means affects the magnitude of the coefficient but not its sign. When weights are independent of the regressors, only their mean values determine the sign. In this case, aligning the mean weights proportionally with the structural effects rules out sign reversal for any covariance structure among the regressors. This protection fails when weights depend on the regressors. A strictly positive and normalized Softmax weighting rule can generate a negative composite coefficient even when the mean weights remain proportional to the structural effects. The results therefore distinguish innocuous weight dispersion from selective weighting related to regressor realizations.

detail.abstract:
Mullin v. Doe (2026) left constitutional claims as the only potential route for challenging the termination of temporary protected status, and it treated the availability of a race-neutral explanation for official statements as decisive against an equal protection claim. Weeks later, a federal district court applying Mullin to Somalia’s designation found a convincing showing of irreparable harm yet no likelihood of success. This Article proposes a doctrinal answer to that impasse, which it calls the diplomatic baseline. Where the government’s own archives preserve an internal, official, specific, and documented characterization of a national group, that record supplies the benchmark animus doctrine has long lacked, because a general policy position cannot explain a reversal confined to one nationality. The Federal Rules of Evidence pose no obstacle because the government’s own statements, offered against it, are statements of an opposing party under Rule 801(d)(2) rather than hearsay.

Drawing on the Public Papers of the Presidents, internal memoranda published in the Foreign Relations of the United States series, the Federal Register, a report transmitted to the Security Council, and contemporaneous State Department and Defense Department records, the Article traces how the United States moved from receiving Somalia as a constitutional peer in 1962 and 1968, through six decades of instrumental engagement under administrations of both parties, to the categorical characterization of Somalis in 2025 and 2026. It then tests the stated rationale for the Somali termination against the government’s own contemporaneous conduct, answers the objections from uniformity, remoteness, changed conditions, selection, and Trump v. Hawaii, and marks the limits of the tool.

The contribution is general and viewpoint neutral. Any litigant, of any national origin and against any administration, may hold the government to its own record.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the state of the Bangsamoro peace process as of 19 September 2026, following the temporary pause in several implementation engagements in March 2026, the resumption of formal bilateral implementation on 4 August 2026, and the first regular Bangsamoro parliamentary election on 14 September 2026. The study asks a question that has become more important as the political transition matures: how should the durability of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB) be understood when the political-institutional track has advanced substantially while the normalization track remains incomplete? Using documentary legal and institutional analysis, the paper examines the CAB and its Annex on Normalization, the Bangsamoro Organic Law, subsequent legislation and executive issuances, official implementation records, independent implementation-monitoring evidence, regional legislation and program records, election-related evidence, and comparative research on peaceagreement implementation and disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration. The evidence supports a mixed but coherent diagnosis. The peace agreement remains operative; autonomous regional institutions have deepened; the first elected Parliament has been proclaimed; and bilateral mechanisms survived a period of political strain. At the same time, final decommissioning remains unfinished, socioeconomic reintegration and camp transformation remain contested or incomplete, and important security, amnesty, and transitional-justice obligations remain in progress. The core problem is therefore neither simple breakdown nor simple completion, but implementation asynchrony: connected obligations have advanced at different rates. Trust is both an input into implementation and an outcome produced by implementation. The paper argues that elections, expenditure, institutional continuity, and numerical decommissioning milestones are important but non-equivalent indicators of substantive normalization. Durable completion requires attention to sequencing, joint implementation, independently verifiable delivery, communitylevel outcomes, and the CAB's own requirement that an Exit Agreement follow full implementation of the agreements.

detail.abstract:
Nigeria has continued to face significant challenges of inadequacy of funding and delayed release of capital budget allocations to Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs) between the year selected 2023 - 2026 which undermine Nigeria's ability to deliver critical infrastructure, public services, and national development priorities. 
Despite annually appropriating multi-trillion-naira budgets in nominal terms, the gap between approved capital expenditure and actual cash-backed releases has weakened project implementation, reduced value for money, and limited the developmental impact of public investments. As stated by Ben Akabueze former Budget Office Director-General to National Assembly policy dialogue in April 2026 over 56,000 government projects remain uncompleted nationwide which reflects not any shortage of development frameworks or ideas, but a deeply entrenched failure to translate approved plans into funded, implemented, and completed outcomes. 
The study identifies revenue underperformance, debt service pressures, weak project prioritization, procurement bottlenecks, fragmented planning systems, and inadequate accountability mechanisms as key drivers of poor capital budget implementation. 
This article reasons that resolving the persistent gap between budget approval and effective budget execution and results delivery requires a comprehensive Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (PMEAL) approach. It traces systematically where each function breaks down, articulates the consequences of those breakdowns, and proposes practical, institution-specific reforms that can realistically build a results-oriented capital budgeting system.
The paper proposes practical results-oriented capital budgeting system centered on sustainable funding mechanisms, strengthening project planning, strengthened monitoring systems, evidence-based evaluation, institutional accountability, and evidence-based learning. The findings suggest that a PMEAL-driven approach can improve budget credibility, ensuring that approved capital projects translate into measurable development outcomes, and contribute to achieving Nigeria's national development plans/objectives.
